We had previously said: if a person among us strives in his work and devotes himself to it for ten years, he lives at ease for the rest of his life; if he strives for twenty years, he gives ease to himself and his children after him; if he strives for thirty years, he gives ease to his grandchildren. So, according to the measure of work is the measure of reward.

Then we must keep in mind the alternation of conditions, and the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And those days We alternate among the people...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 140]. So blessing and expansion of provision are with you today, and they may become another's, or be in the evening.

This verse is the detailed explanation or elaboration of the third verse at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Thus does He reveal to you, and to those before you, Allah, the Almighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Shura: 3]. Detail after summary is one of the methods of the Noble Qur'an.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion﴾... means: He has enacted for you, clarified, and made plain. From this root come shara'a (to prescribe) and shari'ah (the law), meaning a clear way. Man has two aspects: body and spirit. Just as the Truth, glorified is He, has guaranteed the continuation of bodily life through water, food, and air, so He has made life for his spirit through values and morals.

These values are the method of Allah that was sent down upon the heart of His Messenger (ﷺ), and by this method hearts and spirits live just as bodies live by food and drink. This shari'ah and these values are not new in the procession of the messages; rather, they are the sunnah of Allah concerning those who came before: they had a religion and a law, each according to what suited them.

Therefore He said after it: ﴿what He enjoined upon Noah﴾... meaning: what He commanded Noah and obligated him with of duties. He chose Noah because he was the first messenger in the generalities. Some scholars have said that Noah was also sent to all people, on the basis that the people of his time were the passengers of the ark; so the generality of his message was specific to those who were with him on the ark, whereas the generality of the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) was general to people in every place on the face of the earth.

Then reflect on the precision of the Qur'anic expression in ﴿what He enjoined upon Noah﴾. Here "mā" is a relative pronoun meaning "that which." The expected phrasing afterward would have been: "and what We revealed to you." He used the relative pronoun (mā) but here the discourse concerns the revelation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so He said "wa-alladhī" (and that which), which is the mother of all relative pronouns. With the others, "mā" came, which, as the grammarians say, is a relative pronoun meaning "that which." Then notice the verb (waṣṣā) in the singular, whereas with the Messenger of Allah He said: ﴿and that which We revealed to you﴾, with the plural "nūn" which they call the "nūn of majesty."

Then after that the context returns to using (mā) again: ﴿and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus﴾... and this indicates a particularity for our master, the Messenger of Allah, above all the other messengers, peace be upon them all.

Regarding the verbs shara'a and waṣṣā: by what? After them comes (an), which they call the explanatory "an" (an tafsiriyyah), meaning it explains for us the meaning of shara'a and waṣṣā: ﴿that establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾. Similar is His saying: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Moses: suckle him﴾ [al-Qasas: 7]. So: Allah enjoined these prophets to establish the religion and not to be divided or disputed in it.

To establish a thing means to make it standing, and standing is the principal indication of strength and capability, for a person does not stand except in a state of strength. If he tires of standing, he sits; if he tires of sitting, he lies down. So the Truth wants us to make the religion standing, meaning: we stand by it, neither sitting nor sleeping. Thus "standing" here is a metaphor for caring for it and preserving it. ﴿And do not be divided therein﴾ forbids disputing about it...

So His saying, glorified is He: ﴿establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ means: do not take lords besides Allah, or do not split into sects and factions in the religion, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you have no part in them at all﴾ [al-An'am: 159]. Whenever the community is scattered into groups, know that they have all departed from what is right, because the Truth is one, and we must all rally around it.

﴿It is hard upon the polytheists what you call them to﴾... The word kabura with a "u" vowel (kabura) means it became great and burdensome for them, while kabira with an "a" vowel is said of old age. So the polytheists found it great and burdensome what you call them to of monotheism and sincere worship of Allah, Exalted is He. It was hard for them to utter the word of testimony, "there is no god but Allah," although they understood its meaning and its implications well. For them it was not a word that tongues say; rather it is a way of life with requirements; otherwise they would have said it.

It became great in their souls and burdensome for them that people should be equal like the teeth of a comb, with no distinction among them except by piety and righteous deeds. They were the lords, the holders of worldly authority since long ago, so how could Islam come and make the lords and the slaves equal? Thus it was great for them, and it became great in their souls.

Therefore they stood against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), opposed him, and took a stance of contention and enmity. But the Truth, glorified is He, reassures His Messenger, so He says after it: ﴿Allah chooses to Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, reassures His Messenger (ﷺ), saying to him: do not be concerned with their hostile stance toward you or their collision with your call. This is a natural matter; their standing against you is itself a testimony that you are upon the truth, because you will take from them and strip them of the lordship that they had, and prevent the corruption spread in their society, while they benefit from this corruption, and the people are submissive to them because they are weak and have no means.

So: their enmity toward you is a natural matter. They proceed according to their nature and you proceed according to your nature; that is, obstinacy, aggression, and arrogance are among their traits, while bearing harm is among yours.

So His saying: ﴿Allah chooses to Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾ is an indication that these stubborn leaders opposing the call will have among them supporters of it and banners in its sky. So do not hasten, do not grieve, and do not worry. We will bring them into the arena of faith one after another, and indeed Allah was true in what He informed His Messenger: 'Umar, Khalid, 'Amr, 'Ikrimah, and others entered Islam.

The word (yajtabi) means He chooses and selects from among His servants whom He wills to support His religion. This selection is, as it were, a prelude to guidance; therefore He said after it: ﴿and guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾. So He first selects them by keeping them away from enmity toward the call, and makes faith beloved to them, as if preparing them for this task...

Before we leave this verse, we should point out the controversy that some orientalists have raised concerning His saying: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus...﴾ They say: what necessity is there then for the later message, since the commandment to all the messengers is one? Secondly, they claimed there is a contradiction between the verses, because Allah the Exalted said elsewhere: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law and a method﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48].

So: each prophet has a law, and Muhammad has things other than what was enjoined on the others.

To answer the first objection we say: the Truth, glorified is He, has necessary matters which He obligated upon all the messengers in the procession of the messages. They all agree on these matters: first, monotheism and not associating partners with Allah; then faith in the heavenly scriptures and in the messengers; then faith in the resurrection.

These are the common ground of all the messengers, which does not change, because they are the constants of the religion and its pillars, and they are what is meant by His saying: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus...﴾

So the enjoining here concerns the necessary matters that are constant in all the heavenly religions. Monotheism is the call of all Allah's messengers; prayer is found in all the previous laws, and likewise zakah. Therefore it is impossible for any message to be free of these two matters...

Likewise, all the heavenly religions agree on purifying the soul and the limbs from sins and disobedience that harm the self and society, because clearing away sins precedes adorning oneself with acts of obedience.

Take the limbs from the heart down to the foot, and you will find all the heavenly religions calling to purify them. The heart is the leader of the limbs and their sovereign, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said of it: "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Verily, it is the heart."

The heart requires several things: first, not associating partners with Allah; then not persisting in sin; then not feeling secure from Allah's plan and not despairing of Allah's mercy. All of these are beliefs that should settle in the heart.

Likewise the tongue, which is the principal instrument of expression and conveyance, must be purified of several things: first, false testimony; then slandering chaste women; then the perjurious oath (al-yamin al-ghamus), which is an oath with no expiation; then the tongue must be purified from uttering the incantations that sorcerers utter.

Come to the belly: it must be purified and cleared of several things: drinking wine, consuming usury, and consuming the property of orphans.

Likewise the hands must be cleared of theft and killing. Likewise the private parts must be cleared of adultery and other things Allah has forbidden them. Likewise the feet must be cleared of fleeing on the day of battle, and of hastening to everything forbidden.

Among these constants is disobedience to parents, which is forbidden in all religions as well, and it applies to all the limbs. Allah the Truth has forbidden it because honoring one's parents is training and practice in obeying Allah. This is because parents are the direct cause of existence, and Allah, glorified is He, is the indirect cause of existence.

Thus obeying and honoring one's parents is a gateway and an entrance to obeying Allah. And this honor is preserved for them even if they are polytheists: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, and accompany them in this world with kindness﴾ [Luqman: 15].

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, teaches us honoring parents in the entire procession of the messages... So: the Truth wants everyone to be clean and pure of all these sins. Therefore He purified all the limbs and made them instruments of building, affection, and compassion, and built society on upright foundations that guarantee its members a happy and secure life. This is a common factor in all the heavenly religions, and these matters are what is meant by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah...﴾

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law and a method﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48], it means the particular laws and rulings of each religion. These laws differ according to societies, environments, the diseases present, and the afflictions spread among the people. Laws come to treat the afflictions in their society, and therefore they differ from one religion to another...

From this we know that the objection of the orientalists has no basis, for every verse has its own subject.

The Meccan environment contained the Quraysh, who were pagans worshipping idols, and there were also People of the Book, Jews or Christians, and the disagreement between them was ongoing and persistent. Out of anger at the disbelievers, the People of the Book would say to them: "The time of a prophet from among you has drawn near; he will come, and we will follow him and kill you with him, as 'Ad and Iram were killed."

Almighty Allah informs us about the People of the Book: ﴿And they had been, before, seeking victory over those who disbelieved. But when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it..﴾ [al-Baqarah: 89], meaning: Muhammad.

Indeed, the heavenly scriptures gave good tidings of the coming of Muhammad, his time and his place, and the People of the Book knew him and had his attributes with them. Many of them acknowledged that Muhammad was upon the truth and that he was a prophet sent, and among these was Abdullah ibn Salam.

Allah, the Exalted, says about them and their knowledge of the Messenger of Allah by his attributes: ﴿They recognize him as they recognize their own sons..﴾ [al-Baqarah: 146]. Therefore one of them said: "By Allah, I recognize Muhammad as I recognize my son, and my recognition of Muhammad is stronger, because his attributes are mentioned in their books." Yet when he came to them with the truth, they disbelieved in him and opposed him.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And they did not become divided except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves..﴾ [ash-Shura: 14], meaning: the knowledge of him in their books, which gave good tidings of him and mentioned his attributes. ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord..﴾ [ash-Shura: 14], which is His promise, glorified is He, to give them respite ﴿until a specified term..﴾ [ash-Shura: 14], which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the matter would have been decided between them..﴾ [ash-Shura: 14], meaning: it would have been judged between them by the destruction of the disbelievers, their uprooting, and the salvation of the believers. But the Almighty did not decide to destroy and uproot them; rather He delayed them, because there would come from among them one who believes and becomes a soldier from the soldiers of the Truth.

﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them are in disquieting doubt concerning it.﴾ [ash-Shura: 14]. The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture..﴾ are the Jews and Christians contemporary with the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿in doubt concerning it..﴾ [ash-Shura: 14], meaning: concerning their scripture, ﴿disquieting..﴾ [ash-Shura: 14], meaning: it calls to uneasiness, hesitation and bewilderment. This is because they took several courses with their scripture which led them to this doubt and this uneasiness.

First: they forgot part of it, as Allah informed about them: ﴿And from those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of..﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 14], just as He informed about the Jews in the verse before it: ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard; they distort words from their places and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of..﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 13].

Forgetting means not caring about what is forgotten; had it been important, it would have been constantly on their minds and at the center of their concern. And what they did not forget of the Book, they dealt with by distortion. If they had an excuse for forgetting, what is their excuse for distortion?

Then, after that, they concealed what Allah had sent down. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, [He said], "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it." But they threw it behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. And wretched is what they purchase.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 187].

Would that they had stopped at this point in corrupting their Scripture; rather, they went to such excess in corrupting it that they composed speech from themselves and said, "It is from Allah." Allah, the Exalted, says concerning them: ﴿So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say, "This is from Allah," to exchange it for a small price. So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 79].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 15:

The allusion in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So for that [reason], invite [them], and remain steadfast as you have been commanded﴾ [al-Shura: 15], refers back to the preceding discourse: since they have split into factions, disagreed, concealed the Book and distorted it, then, as long as they have done that, you, [O Prophet], must take up the task of the call (da'wah) to set right what these people have corrupted, to establish the balance of life upon truth and justice, and to turn these people back from what they are engaged in.

Note here that the expression combines speech and action: ﴿So invite, and remain steadfast as you have been commanded﴾ [al-Shura: 15]. That is: let your words be consistent with your conduct, as He said in another place: ﴿Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast﴾ [Fussilat: 30].

We have already said that the straight line is the shortest path between two points. So istiqamah (steadfastness) means: remain on the highway and on the right path. The Qur'an has called it (al-Sirat al-Mustaqim) [the Straight Path], and called it (sawa' al-sabil) [the even way], which is what brings you to your goal by the shortest route.

So it is as if the Almighty, when He commands His Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, to do this, is saying to him: "Be steadfast, for your steadfastness upon the method you have brought is more conducive to acceptance, to their believing you, and to their listening to you."

It is well known that teaching and advice through action are more beneficial and more useful than theoretical speech. Therefore, when one of the Companions asked the Messenger of Allah, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me in Islam a saying about which I will not ask anyone after you," he said to him: "[Say, "I believe in Allah," then remain steadfast]." This is one of the comprehensive sayings (jawami' kalimihi) of his, peace be upon him.

After his Lord commanded him to be steadfast upon the method of truth, He forbade him from following the desires of the people: ﴿And do not follow their desires﴾ [al-Shura: 15]. For desire is the path of disagreement and division. Among these desires is their saying to the Messenger of Allah: "You worship our gods for a year, and we worship your God for a year." And concerning this, Surat al-Kafirun was revealed.

﴿And say, "I have believed in what Allah has sent down of Book﴾ [al-Shura: 15]. "Book" here is an indefinite noun that conveys comprehensiveness; that is: I believe in every book that Allah has sent down before.

It is as if this is a message to the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians: Why did you believe in the religions before you, but did not believe in the message of Muhammad, which is a religion like the other religions? So, you have precedence in faith; why, then, did you stop at my message and deny it? They denied it because they have matters with which they dispute the weak among the Muslims.

For example, they say to them: "Our religion is older than yours, our book is older than yours, our messenger is older than yours, and your Qur'an bears witness to us. Did not the Qur'an say: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds﴾ [al-Baqarah: 122]? So we are, then, preferred over the worlds by the testimony of the Qur'an."

The preference here is not absolute, but is restricted to their time. That is: I preferred you over the worlds of your people's time; otherwise they would be better than Abraham and Isaac, and they do not say that.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And I have been commanded to act justly between you﴾ [al-Shura: 15]. Justice is that you weigh with a scale that is not unjust, so that each one of them takes his right, and that all of them are equal before you. For example, you do not rebuke one and leave the other, nor do you favor one over another in your sight, in your gathering, or in your regard.

For this reason, when he, peace be upon him, sat among his Companions, he would distribute his gaze among all of them, so that he did not give attention to one to the exclusion of the other.

All of them were equal before him; had he given special attention to one particular person, he would have been thought to have a superiority, or a worldly authority, or a central power. Never were they, in his sight, other than equal. All of these are part of his justice, peace be upon him, among people.

And His saying: ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord﴾ [al-Shura: 15]. That is: He is not our Lord alone; He is also your Lord. Since He is our Lord and your Lord, the nurturing must be one for all of us. He has sent down to you a method for a time, and He has sent down to me a final method.

And from the perfection of this nurturing: ﴿For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds﴾ [al-Shura: 15]. Each is recompensed for his deed. ﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾ [al-Shura: 15]: no disputation and no debate. Why? Because debate with them leads to contention, obstinacy and enmity, and does not lead to the truth. The meaning is: we will not meet, for each of us has his own path.

The Almighty has addressed this matter in Surat (al-Kafirun): ﴿Say, "O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshippers of what I worship, nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."﴾ [al-Kafirun: 1-6].

So: there is no room for debate, because the matter is settled. Politics has taught us that states may differ and sever relations with one another, then the circumstances of life compel them to restore relations again and to make peace. But in the matter of faith and disbelief, they are opposites that can never possibly meet.

Therefore, when you examine Surat al-Kafirun, you find that it negates this meeting in the present and in the future. Read: ﴿I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾ [al-Kafirun: 2-3], that is, in the present; ﴿Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ [al-Kafirun: 4-6], that is, in the future.

And His saying: ﴿Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the destination﴾ [al-Shura: 15]. That is: since we have not come together upon the truth in this world, Allah will gather us all on the Day of Resurrection for judgment, where each will be recompensed for his deed, and each one of rightful claim will be given his right. As for your referring the matter to a just arbiter, this is evidence that you are upon the truth, and Allah is sufficient as a judge. ﴿And to Him is the destination﴾ [al-Shura: 15]: the return and the final place of return.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 16:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who argue about Allah...﴾ [al-Shura: 16], meaning they dispute concerning the religion of Allah. Who do they dispute with? They dispute with those who have responded to the call of truth ﴿after it has been accepted...﴾ [al-Shura: 16]. They say to them: "Our religion is older than your religion, and our messenger is older than your messenger, and the Qur'an testifies for us that we are the best of the worlds." By that disputation they intend to turn them back from their faith.

As for these people, ﴿their argument is void with their Lord...﴾ [al-Shura: 16], meaning: it is a false argument that is not accepted by Allah the Exalted, and it is never proper to pay attention to it. ﴿And upon them is wrath...﴾ [al-Shura: 16], that is: wrath from Allah. Why? Because they were not content to be disbelievers themselves; rather they wanted to draw others into disbelief, and by that they bear their own burdens and the burdens of those whom they misled. Thus they deserved this destiny, which is the wrath of Allah upon them, and wrath is the first stage of punishment.

Therefore, in a sacred hadith (hadith qudsi), the Truth, glorified is He, described the state of a group upon whom Allah's wrath descended; then He commanded a veil to be placed between them and Him, then He cursed them, then He expelled them from His mercy, the Exalted. To clarify this matter, we say, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude: a man who owns a company in which there are employees and workers. One of them committed an error that angered the owner of the company, so his heart changed toward him, yet he left him in his job. Then he committed another error, and he said to him: "Keep away from me; do not make me see your face," as if he had set a barrier between them so that he would not see him. Then, in the final stage, he said: "This employee must surely be dismissed from work."

Likewise, the Truth, glorified is He, became angry with these people, then a veil was set between them and Him, then He cursed them, then He expelled them from His mercy, the Exalted. ﴿And for them is a severe punishment﴾ [al-Shura: 16], that is: in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 17:

His saying, Most High: ﴿with the truth﴾. The truth (al-haqq) is the thing that is established and does not change, and the truth is victorious without doubt. If falsehood (al-batil) rises over it for a period of time, that is only for a wisdom, which is that falsehood bites people so as to charge them with zeal for the truth and make them yearn for it. So the final outcome belongs to the truth, however long falsehood lasts, attacks and roams freely. Therefore we have said: falsehood is a soldier among the soldiers of the truth.

Now read this image which the Truth, glorified be He, drew to clarify for us the truth and falsehood. He, Most High, says: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from what they heat in the fire, seeking an ornament or a commodity, there is a foam like it. Thus does God strike the truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum; but as for what benefits people, it remains on the earth. Thus does God strike the parables﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17].

So the truth is what remains, and falsehood is what vanishes and perishes...

And His saying: (and the Balance). He mentioned a tangible thing, which is the balance (al-mizan), and the balance is the instrument for establishing the truth... So the word "mizan" means the controls that regulate between truth and falsehood. We read in surah al-Hadid: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance, that people may uphold justice﴾ [al-Hadid: 25]. That is: with justice and truth. So the Balance came to give every person with a right his right, and to regulate rights for their owners, so that no one takes more than his right, no one usurps the right of another, and no one covets what is not his.

And His, glorified be He, saying: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ because they had previously asked the Messenger to bring it, as the Qur'an relates of them: ﴿They say, "When will this promise be, if you are truthful?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 38]; they asked for it in a manner of mockery, derision and denial of it. The verb "daraa" (to know) in the form yadri appears once in the present tense here, ﴿wa-ma yudrika﴾, and appears in the past tense in His saying: ﴿The Inevitable Reality. What is the Inevitable Reality? And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?﴾ [al-Haqqah: 1-3].

The meaning of ﴿wa-ma adraka﴾ [al-Haqqah: 3] in the past tense is a thing of old which you did not know from before, but you know it now. As for ﴿wa-ma yudrika﴾, it means: no one informs you of it except Us: ﴿None but He will reveal it at its time﴾ [al-A'raf: 187]. As for the future form, it never came.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 42, verse 18:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: "Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it." That is, they seek to hasten the Hour (al-Sa'ah). Because they do not know it, do not believe in it, and do not know what takes place in it, they ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for it, saying to him: "Bring us this Resurrection, we want to see it." This is said mockingly. Had they known anything of its terrors, they would not have dared to demand it, nor would they have made light of it. This is the condition of those who do not affirm the Day of Resurrection.

As for the believers in it, they have a different state: "And those who believe are apprehensive of it," fearful of its terrors, because of what they know of its truth, the precision of the reckoning within it, and the severity of its distress. "And they know that it is the truth." He did not say "a truth" but said "the truth" (al-Haqq), meaning: it is the truth itself. There is no room in it for denial, nor even for doubt about its matter.

Therefore, those who dispute about it in mere argument are described as being "in far error": "Verily, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in far error." Al-Mira' (mira') is vain disputation that does not lead to the truth.

He described them as being in far error because rational reflection alone establishes the Day of Resurrection and its necessity with respect to the life of this world. If they reflected upon the reality of their lives, they would find that in their worldly affairs they adopt the principle of reward and punishment, for affairs cannot be set right without repaying the good-doer for his goodness and punishing the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing.

In the reality of their lives there are teachers and pupils in schools who hold monthly examinations in which mistakes are marked in red so that the pupil may know his error and correct it. But in the end-of-year examination, mistakes are not marked; rather, a grade is given on which success or failure depends. This is accountability and recompense.

So if you do this in your worldly affairs, why do you deny it with regard to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? In humanity, on the journey of life, there are the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient, the criminal and the benefactor. How, then, could all of these be equal?

The man who said: "The oppressor will never die until Allah takes vengeance upon him" spoke because reason says so, and it is not right that he should escape his crimes without punishment. When he saw an oppressor die safe, untouched by anything, what did he say? He said: "There must be behind this world another life in which the oppressor is punished for his oppression. There must be, otherwise the criminal oppressors have triumphed and escaped with their crimes, and the right of the wronged and the weak has been lost both in this world and in the Hereafter."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 19:

The meaning of ﴿Al-Latif...﴾ [al-Shura: 19] is: gentle in dealing with His servants, who pardons much and does not hold His servant to account for the first offence. For this reason, when they brought before Umar a woman who had stolen, she said to him: "By God, I had not stolen before this, and this is the first time." So he said to her: "You are lying. God would not expose you for a first offence." And the Exalted and Majestic says: ﴿And He pardons much﴾ [al-Shura: 30], meaning: He pardons many of your misdeeds and does not hold you to account except for those that are evident among them.

Among the meanings of al-Latif is that He is the Subtle One who penetrates into things. We have already said regarding material things that the smaller and finer a thing becomes, the more it penetrates and the harder it is to guard against. We gave an example of this: a man who built a house in the open countryside and placed on the windows a mesh of iron that keeps out wolves and wild beasts, then found in the environment flies and mosquitoes, so he brought another mesh that is finer and narrower.

Likewise, among His attributes, may He be exalted, is that He is al-Latif, meaning that nothing veils itself from Him, and nothing is hidden from Him, however fine or small it may be. We say of a refined person of good character: "So-and-so is latif," meaning gentle in dealing.

Among His gentleness towards us, may He be glorified, is that He made repentance acceptable to us, and made for us seasons of worship in which good deeds are multiplied and bad deeds are erased, as if they were (clearance sales) for obedience and the gaining of good deeds. Among His gentleness, may He be exalted, towards us is that He made the reward of a good deed ten times its like up to seven hundredfold, whereas a bad deed is counted as one.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty﴾ [al-Shura: 19]. He provides because He is the Creator, and He, glorified, is the One who brought this creation into being, so He undertook to provide for it. He, glorified, is the Strong, because gentleness can only come from strength. He, glorified, is the Mighty, the Victorious, from whom nothing can escape and whom nothing can overcome.

The surface meaning of the word al-harth (ḥarth, tillage) is ploughing the land with the plough and stirring it up for the sowing of seed in it. This is because the young plant cannot break through hard soil, so the soil is broken up for it to make its growth easier; then it needs air, and tillage turns the soil over and allows air to penetrate it.

Since tillage is the cause of the fruit, the word was applied to the fruit: al-harth means the desired produce of the crop. From it is His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And Allah does not like corruption.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 205], and His saying: ﴿And David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the tilth (al-harth) when the sheep of a people had grazed therein at night...﴾ [al-Anbiya': 78], meaning: in the crop.

So the meaning of: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth...﴾ [al-Shura: 20] is: its everlasting reward and its eternal bliss in the Gardens of Eden. Allah, exalted be He, clarifies religious matters for us through images drawn from the reality of our lives, to bring them closer to understanding. Consider, for example: ﴿Certainly will the believers have succeeded﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 1]. Whoever succeeds is like one who ploughs the land and prepares it for cultivation; he is about to gather the fruit. Likewise the believer has attained everlasting reward and lasting bliss.

﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth...﴾ [al-Shura: 20] means: he finds in the Hereafter more than he was expecting, and he is also not deprived of its fruit in this world. ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him thereof...﴾ [al-Shura: 20], meaning: of the fruits of this world. A person is not deprived of the fruit of his effort and toil in this world: ﴿Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of one who does good work﴾ [al-Kahf: 30].

Whoever works for this world is not deprived of its enjoyment and pleasure, but when good things are hastened for him in this world, he is deprived of them in the Hereafter: ﴿and he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Shura: 20], meaning he has no portion in the reward of the Hereafter, because he worked in his worldly life for status, fame, wealth or riches. Whoever takes the means to something attains it, even if he is a disbeliever in Allah; and the believer, if he is lax and sits idle from striving, is deprived because he did not take the means.

Allah, exalted be He, accepts from deeds only what was done sincerely for Him. Whoever desires the tilth of this world, Allah has never been in his mind. Therefore people often ask about the scholars and inventors who served humanity with their inventions and discoveries: what is their fate? We say: their fate is the Fire, because they worked for humanity and not for Allah; they worked for fame, and they received it in this world.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 42, verse 21:

Meaning: Why did they deny Muhammad and not believe in what he brought? Do they have partners who laid down for them a law (shar') and a method (manhaj) to follow, and a religion (din) to adhere to, abandoning the religion of Muhammad? The "partners" are the things they worshipped besides God. Some of them worshipped the sun, some the moon, the tree, the stone, or the angels. Do these supposed deities have any law? Did they say to them: "Do this and do not do that"?

Therefore: deities without a method and without obligations, whose worship is false, and they only worshipped them for that reason, because they have no method and no obligations. They merely satisfy the desire for religiosity that is in their souls. And how easy it is for a person to have a religion without obligations. Worship is nothing other than the worshipper's obedience to the one worshipped in its commands and prohibitions. Then, what did these objects of worship prepare for those who obeyed them, and what did they prepare for those who disobeyed them?

Therefore: these are inanimate things that did not say anything to you, did not command you with anything, and did not legislate a religion for you. Rather, you legislated for yourselves and followed your desires to satisfy an emotion in your souls. Your gods are the work of your hands or your sick, misguided thoughts.

For this reason, God, exalted is He, says: ﴿God did not ordain any bahira, nor sa'iba, nor wasila, nor ham; but those who disbelieve invent lies against God, and most of them do not reason﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 103].

Indeed, these are a people who invent lies against God and fabricate from themselves things for which God has sent down no authority. So from where did they get the bahira, the sa'iba, the wasila and the ham? These are things they invented from themselves, a fabrication and a lie against God...

﴿And had it not been for a prior decree...﴾ That is: the ruling that they would not be destroyed and that their punishment would be deferred to the Hereafter, ﴿they would have been judged between them﴾, meaning: they would have been sentenced to immediate punishment.

When we look at the things God has made lawful and the things He has made unlawful, we find that they rest upon considering benefit and repelling harm from the human being. The lawful contains benefit and the unlawful contains harm...

Then we note in the verse that it expressed their falsehood, which they brought from themselves, as a religion: ﴿Or do they have partners who have legislated for them of the religion...﴾. So falsehood was called "religion" by extension, because they believe in it and regard it as a religion, as God says: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ [al-Kafirun: 6], according to their belief. And religion (din) is that to which a person submits himself.

﴿And indeed, for the wrongdoers there is a painful punishment.﴾ The wrongdoer either wrongs another or wrongs himself, and this is the most abominable kind of wrongdoing. Is it conceivable that a person wrongs his enemy, yet wrongs his own self that lies between his two sides?! How, then, does a person wrong himself? He wrongs it when he exposes it to punishment and deprives it of reward and bliss. The gravest form of a person's wronging himself is to wrong it in the matter of creed and faith in God: ﴿Indeed, associating partners with God is a tremendous wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 22:

The word ﴿You see﴾ [al-Shura: 22] indicates everything from which seeing can proceed. ﴿Fearful﴾ [al-Shura: 22] means afraid and terrified. ﴿Of what they earned﴾ [al-Shura: 22] means of what they did of evil deeds. We have said: the verb kasaba (to earn) yaksibu means an increase over the capital, that is, profit, and that it always comes in earning good; as for iktasaba, it is on the pattern ifta'ala, which carries the sense of effort and attempt, and it comes in evil. But here kasaba is used for evil deeds.

As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Yes, whoever earns an evil deed and his sin surrounds him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 81]. They said: kasaba is used here because the evil deed has become for him a habit and a natural matter, similar to the doing of good for the people of good. He does the evil deed and it does not tire him, because he has become accustomed to it.

His saying: ﴿Fearful of what they earned﴾ [al-Shura: 22] is a depiction of their situation on the Day of Resurrection, because in the world they did not fear and did not take account of this day. ﴿And it will surely befall them﴾ [al-Shura: 22] means: there is no doubt in that, because it is the promise of Allah and His judgment which He has told of.

Or (it means) fearful while they are still in the ease of this world. In this is evidence of the existence of conscience and the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah) in man. He knows the evil deed and knows his crime, and knows that he will be held accountable for it, therefore he fears it and his conscience rebukes him.

In contrast: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in the gardens of the Gardens; for them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty﴾ [al-Shura: 22]. This is a report from Allah, exalted is He, and it is true. The outcome of faith and righteous deeds is the gardens of the Gardens, meaning their delights and the best of their places, which they will find on the Day of Resurrection; and they find them even in this world through imagining them and longing for them.

So the martyr who gives his soul in the way of Allah does not proceed to that except through his certainty in this bliss, and that if he is killed in the way of Allah he will go to something better than this life.

We have mentioned, why? Because he is certain of the truth of the reward in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 169].

Yes, the martyrs are alive, and alive with whom? With their Lord. This is the peak of honor, might and bliss, and it is a distinction which none other has attained. Martyrdom has transported them from one life to another, so they do not die after that, and they are resurrected with the people while they are alive.

The poet expressed this meaning when he said about the master of martyrs, Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

O Hamzah, uncle of the Chosen One, you are a master
over all the martyrs of the earth, all of them entirely.

And it suffices you of that martyrdom a protection from death, in joining the two lives to the other.

His saying: ﴿in the gardens of the Gardens﴾ [al-Shura: 22]. Rawdat is the plural of rawdah, which is the garden or orchard full of greenery, freshness, flowers and fruits, such that when you enter it, its fragrant aroma breathes upon you, and in its midst are rivers flowing with sweet water.

So those who believed and did righteous deeds in the gardens of the Gardens means: in the best and most excellent of their places. ﴿For them is whatever they wish with their Lord﴾ [al-Shura: 22]. This being-with (al-'indiyyah) is more honorable and greater than any other bliss, for they are in the bliss of the Gardens and its delights, and above all of that is that they are with their Lord. Therefore He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿That is the great bounty﴾ [al-Shura: 22], meaning: a favor from Allah and a generosity upon them.

When one of us reflects on this lasting, enduring bliss which the Truthful, glorified is He, has prepared for His believing servants, every hardship of acts of obedience and worship becomes easy for him, and he sees that they are light when compared with the reward for them.

A person toils in this world and strives in seeking knowledge for dozens of years, or in learning a craft or profession, bearing its difficulties and dangers, all to secure for himself merely the necessities of life. If he strives more, sweats and exerts great effort, he may perhaps reach a stage of comfort, so that he has a servant who serves him, or a cook, for example, who prepares food for him. These work for him for a wage, and perhaps they fall short in their work, and perhaps they anger you and rebel against you.

But when you work for the Hereafter, you find the matter entirely different. Worship is light in its matter; it does not require from you all this effort, this sweat, sleepless nights, daytime labor, and preoccupation of mind and intellect. And despite its ease and simplicity, the reward for it is great, without limit, and beyond what comes to mind.

We have said: the utmost that mankind has reached in scientific progress in fields of hotel service, for example, is that you press a button on a machine from which tea or coffee comes down for you, and this machine may break down, while behind it is a worker who prepares the tea or coffee for you. But in Paradise the bliss there is pure, not disturbed by anything, and lasting, never ceasing. It does not require from you any request, nor pressing a button, nor calling a servant; merely the thing occurring to your mind, you find it before your hands. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke truly. Read, for example, in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a fruit therefrom as provision, they will say, "This is what we were provided with before," and they are given it in resemblance; and for them therein are purified spouses, and they will abide therein eternally﴾ [al-Baqarah: 25].

In Paradise, God willing, we will find things which we used to eat in this world, and we imagine they are like the bliss of this world, but when we taste them we find them to be something else. ﴿They will say, "This is what we were provided with before," and they are given it in resemblance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 25]. That is because the perfections of Allah, glorified is He, have no end, so it does not remain in one monotonous state, rather in it there is an ascent in bounty.

So then: we are before an enduring bliss for which every fatigue and every hardship becomes easy. By Allah, if there were no reward for obedience except the safety and happiness of a person in this world, it would be sufficient; from obedience we have the ease of mind, calm of soul and tranquility. The poet expressed this meaning, saying:

The astrologer and the physician, both of them said: "The bodies will not be resurrected." I said to you both:

If your saying is correct, I will not be a loser; but if my saying is correct, the loss will be upon you both.

Therefore, when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wished to describe Paradise for us, He did not describe Paradise itself, but rather gave an example of it, because Paradise and what is in it are beyond human imagination. If there is in it what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and nor has it occurred to the heart of a human, then how can it be described to us as it truly is? Because a person only assigns a word to a known referent; as for a thing we do not know, we consequently do not know the word that signifies it. There are no words in our language that describe this bliss. Therefore read: ﴿The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised...﴾ [al-Ra'd: 35], wherein are such and such.

Moreover, this lasting bliss is a reward for whom? For those who believe and resolve to join faith with righteous deeds. The Qur'an always pairs faith with righteous deeds. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but rejoice in Paradise, which you were promised"﴾ [Fussilat: 30].

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿That is what Allah gives good news of...﴾.

That is the blessing of Paradise. ﴿That of which God gives good tidings to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds...﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23]. Glad tidings (bishara) means informing someone of good before its time.

Then the context moves to another matter, concerning the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the matter of the call (da'wa). ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it...﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23]. The meaning is: Say to them, O Muhammad, that I do not want from you any reward for the call and the mission that I carry out for your sake. You would not say this word unless you had actually done a work for which you deserved a reward.

So the meaning is as if he is saying: the work that I do for your sake ought to have a reward due to me, because I advise you and guide you to what benefits you, and yet I do not want any reward from you.

All the Messengers of God said this word, because a person customarily repays one who has done him a kindness, or guided him to good, or offered him counsel that brings him comfort. Therefore, in many accounts of the messages we read: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for any wealth for it; my reward is only from God...﴾ [Hud: 29]. Yes, from God. Why? Because it is a great, precious and noble work, which no human can value as it deserves, or give the reward it merits. So: none will give me my reward except God who sent me.

We said: all the Messengers said this word except our master Ibrahim and our master Musa, peace be upon them both. Why? They said: because our master Ibrahim, when he first called, called his father Azar, so how could he ask him for a reward? Likewise, our master Musa, when he first called, called Pharaoh, and Pharaoh had a favour over him in upbringing.

So: I do not want from you any reward for the mission of the call that I carry out; my reward for it is from God who sent me, and He is the One who values it as it deserves. There is one thing I want from you: ﴿except affection for the near of kin...﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23], meaning your affection for my kinship. Affection (mawadda) is the inclination of the heart toward one whom you love, and then treating him with the honour and esteem he deserves.

So it is as if the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is saying to them: I have been sent to all people, and you have met me with harm, confronted me with hostility, and persecuted my companions. You forced me to turn to others, once to Ta'if, and once to the other tribes; and you forced my companions to leave their lands and homes. And I have kinship with every clan of Quraysh, and even in Medina, where my maternal uncles are from Banu al-Najjar. So at least give me my right in my kinship, and the right of kinship is that you do not harm me. I do not compel you to Islam, nor do I do anything that calls for harm. Likewise, it is among the rights of kinship that you do not hand me over to my enemy. This is my right over you.

Or the meaning may be: ﴿except affection for the near of kin...﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23], meaning my relatives and the People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt). This is because the relatives of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were deprived of a helper in livelihood, so they are not like the rest of the Muslims, since the zakat (obligatory almsgiving) funds that a poor person from others would receive were forbidden to them. So at least treat them with goodness and kindness, and observe their status with me.

Therefore we find many hadiths on honouring the People of the House, which others say were said by others. Among them: Whoever dies loving the family of the Messenger of God dies a martyr; dies forgiven; dies with the angels greeting him in his grave; dies with a gate in his grave leading him to Paradise. And whoever hates the family of Muhammad is despairing of the mercy of God.

They said this because the Prophet (ﷺ) said words like this. He said: and this is another meaning of ﴿except affection for the near of kin...﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23].

Or a third meaning is intended: ﴿except affection for the near of kin...﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23], meaning your own kin: each one of you should love his relative, give to him, and observe the right of his kinship. If every person who has a surplus of provision gave to his relatives, supported them and helped them to a dignified livelihood, there would not be found among us any poor or needy person. Society is a set of overlapping circles, so if we did that, the goodness of God would spread to all of God's creation.

Furthermore, relatives have a right in your wealth beyond zakat. Therefore one of the wealthy said: I give my poor brother from the zakat money. We said to him: By God, if he knew that you give him from zakat money, he would not accept it. So give him from the 97.5% and not from the 2.5%. Leave this small percentage for the distant poor who are far from you.

Another says: I put zakat money into building a school; another says: into building a hospital or a mosque. Glory be to God! Does 2.5% suffice for all this? Make it for its rightful recipients as God prescribed it, so that the state of society may be upright. Then, if we did all this from zakat money, what would we do with the 97.5%?

Placing zakat money in its proper place, as the Truthful One (may He be glorified) taught us, protects society and conceals its faults. You will not find in it a naked person, a hungry person, or a sick person who cannot find the cost of treatment. But when we disabled the provisions of the Sharia in this matter, the faults of the Muslim society appeared, as we see and witness.

The Truthful One, glorified and exalted, distributed His goodness among all His creation and "engineered" the economy of society, so that if His teachings were implemented in this matter, the poor would live at the same standard of living as the rich.

From this justice in distributing goodness among people, you find, for example, a wealthy man in a town which has been his homeland since birth, yet he longs for another homeland, goes there, builds and prospers in it, and overflows with his goodness upon its people. They said: when you see such a man, know that his presence is in excess of the needs of his own town, so God transferred him to another place that needs him.

And if we do this with our relatives, then the Messenger of God has more right over the believers than their own selves, so the kinship of the Messenger of God has the greater claim. This is because the Messenger of God knew that there would come periods in which his family would be persecuted, and history bears witness to this. You have seen the People of the House scattered across all lands, and some of them killed. You know the extent of the love of the people of Egypt for the People of the House of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Likewise we love Abu Bakr and Umar, and there is not a single Shi'i among us.

Affection and kinship, when they first exist, exist for God the Exalted and for His Messenger (ﷺ). If affection is the inclination of the heart toward whom you desire, then this inclination has consequences. So you do not see him in need while you have means, nor see him ignorant while you are learned, and so on.

From affection within kinship is dutifulness to parents. We have said: the Truthful One, glorified and exalted, made dutifulness to parents a training and discipline for faith in God, because they are the direct cause of existence, and He, glorified be He, is the supreme cause of existence. He, glorified be He, said: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents...﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 8], and in another verse: ﴿We have enjoined upon man to be good to his parents...﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 15].

Even in the case of their disobedience, in the highest domain, which is the domain of creed and monotheism, He commanded their honouring: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them; but accompany them in this world with kindness...﴾ [Luqman: 15]. He gave the greatest attention to the mother in His saying: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man to be good to his parents...﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 8], meaning both of them, and He did not mention a reason for the father; rather He mentioned the reason of the mother, saying: ﴿His mother carried him in weakness upon weakness...﴾ [Luqman: 14]. This is because the role of the mother was during childhood, when one has not yet reasoned about what she does. Her role is hidden from you, preceding your awareness and understanding of matters. When you grew up, you recognized the role of the father; therefore the Truthful One reminded you of the role of the mother that had been hidden from you.

Then we find the Qur'an being cautious and observing the right of upbringing, to the extent that if someone other than the parents raised you, it says: ﴿And say: My Lord, have mercy on them as they brought me up when I was small﴾ [Al-Isra: 24]. So whoever raised you holds the rank of the parents and deserves dutifulness just as they do, exactly.

His saying: ﴿And whoever earns a good deed...﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23], meaning: performs an act of obedience to God, ﴿We will increase for him therein in goodness...﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23]. So the matter does not stop at the limit of affection; rather you also look after them in what they need. ﴿Indeed, God is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾ [Ash-Shura: 23]. "Forgiving" and "Appreciative" are intensive forms of "forgiver" and "thankful." So the Truthful One is abundant in forgiveness and much in appreciation: He forgives whoever turns to Him in repentance, and appreciates whoever obeys Him. Appreciation takes the form of increase, as He said: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you...﴾ [Ibrahim: 7].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (*Tafsir al-Sha'rawi*, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 24:

The discussion here concerns the disbelievers of Makkah, who accused the Messenger of God (ﷺ) of fabricating the Qur'an himself and attributing it to God. ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against God"?﴾ That is, the disbelievers say he brought the Qur'an from himself. Yet the fabrication (al-iftira') came from them, for they were the people of speech, the masters of odes and sermons, and they knew nothing of Muhammad, though he lived among them, that he had any distinction in this field.

So: you are the people of this art, and your tongues are long. Why, then, did you not produce something like it, even a single surah? If fabrication were true of Muhammad, you would be more entitled to it. Why did the Qur'an challenge you and you produced nothing? Not ten surahs, nor even one surah.

In another place, the Qur'an answers them with logic and gentle reason: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say: "If I have invented it, upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit."﴾ (Hud 11:35).

Therefore, the context of the verse shifts from speaking about the disbelievers and their fabrication against the Messenger to addressing the Messenger directly: ﴿If God willed, He would seal upon your heart﴾. That is: if it had happened from you that you fabricated the Qur'an and brought it from yourself, God is able to seal your heart, O Muhammad, so that you would forget what you memorise. Did that happen to the Messenger of God (ﷺ)? No, rather the Qur'an remained in his breast, he recited it in the hours of the night and the ends of the day, and he taught it to the people.

So: Muhammad did not deny the Qur'an, nor did he fabricate against God; rather, you are the fabricators. In many places the Qur'an exposes their fabrication and answers them with reason, logic and what is better. It recounts how they clung to this matter: ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him."﴾ (al-Nahl 16:103). They accused the Messenger of frequenting a foreign man who taught him the Qur'an, so the Truthful Lord replies: ﴿The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ (al-Nahl 16:103).

The man you say Muhammad frequents to learn the Qur'an is a foreigner, while the Qur'an is in clear Arabic. Where, then, are your minds? And if you are a liar, then at least be a good liar, so that your falsehood and deceit are not exposed.

The Qur'an recounts another form of their obstinacy and stubbornness: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it." Say: "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I follow only what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day."﴾ (Yunus 10:15). ﴿Say: "If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you know it. I lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not reason?"﴾ (Yunus 10:16).

Yes, Muhammad brought the Qur'an after he was forty, while he was among them. They never saw him as an orator or a poet, and nothing of that kind was known of him.

When they despaired, they said: the Qur'an is not bad, but its flaw is that it was sent down upon Muhammad in particular: ﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man of the two cities?"﴾ (al-Zukhruf 43:31).

Then the Truthful Lord exposes their position, shows their foolishness and their obstinacy in falsehood, and that this dispute is nothing but stubbornness and arrogance against accepting the truth. He says: ﴿And when they said, "O God, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ (al-Anfal 8:32). Is this the speech of sensible people, or is it hatred of Muhammad himself?

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And God will erase falsehood and establish truth by His words﴾ (al-Shura 42:24). The verb yamhu (erases) has its waw deleted for lightness, and what is erased is the falsehood they uttered, and the fabrication they attributed falsely to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). God erases this. In contrast, wa-yuhiqqu al-haqq ("and establishes the truth") means He confirms and strengthens it, bi-kalimatihi ("by His words"), that is, what was sent down upon the heart of our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), in the noble Qur'an.

Or the words may mean the word kun ("Be!") and it is, ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, that is, He knows the hidden things which a person cannot express with his tongue, so he conceals them in his intention and in himself, as He, glorified is He, says: ﴿He knows the deceit of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ (Ghafir 40:19).

So these people continued to oppose the Messenger of God (ﷺ), to harbour hatred against him, to confront his call and to accuse him, until God exposed their falsehood and eliminated it. Their affair ended either in Islam, or in defeat, or they were covered by the pardon of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the day of the conquest of Makkah, when he said to them: "What do you think I will do with you?" They said: "Good, a noble brother and the son of a noble brother." He said: "Go, for you are the freed ones (al-Tulaqa')."

So the help of God and the conquest came, falsehood vanished, truth was established, rose high and triumphed. Is it conceivable that God would send a Messenger to guide creation, then hand him over to his enemies, or abandon him in his confrontation with falsehood?

God the Exalted says: ﴿And Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the victorious. And indeed, Our soldiers – they will be the predominant.﴾ (al-Saffat 37:171-173).

Finally, we note on this verse that some thought the verb yamhu is conjoined to (yashya') and that it is jussive (majzum) like it after the conditional particle in, and this is not correct. The verb "yamhu" came as a new, independent statement, as evidenced by the repetition of the divine name (Allah) and the nominative case of "wa-yuhiqqu" (and establishes). It is a verb in the indicative (marfu') mood, and the waw was deleted for lightness, or to avoid two consecutive unvocalised letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 42, verse 25:

It is among the gentleness of Allah toward His servants and His mercy to them that He prescribed repentance (tawbah) for them and made its door open, never to be closed. Repentance is a hope to which the one who has done wrong clings, and in it he finds the rope of salvation, so he returns, his conduct improves, his behaviour is set right, and his community benefits from him. But if we shut the door of repentance in his face and drive him to despair, he persists in his disobedience, and he becomes wretched and his community becomes wretched along with him.

Repentance means the return of the wrongdoer to Allah, and it has stages. Allah prescribed repentance, and the mere prescribing of it is a bounty from Allah. Then, when the servant repents, Allah accepts his repentance. Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent﴾ [al-Tawbah: 118]. That is: He prescribed repentance for them so that they would repent, and then accept their repentance.

Repentance is not a phrase that is said: "I ask Allah's forgiveness, the Mighty, there is no god but Him, and I repent to Him." Rather, repentance is a complete method (manhaj). Imam ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, explained this when the iqamah for prayer was called and he heard a man in the row saying: "I ask Allah's forgiveness, the Mighty," "Allahu akbar." When the man finished the prayer, ʿAli said to him: "You hastened in repentance; your repentance itself needs repentance."

So: it is not merely a word, but a method and a programme in which you first review the evil deeds that have passed you by and the negligence that has come from you, so you first feel remorse (nadam) for what has issued from you. It has been reported in a hadith: "Remorse is repentance."

And in the story of the children of Adam: ﴿So his soul permitted him the murder of his brother, and he killed him, and he became among the losers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 30]. When the surge of evil and enmity subsided in him, he returned to what was right and regretted what he had done. Then you remember the obligatory prayers you missed, and you make them up or compensate for them with voluntary prayers (nawafil).

Then you return the wrongs (mazalim) to their owners. These are conditions that must be fulfilled. Beyond that, you should melt into good deeds just as you melted into evil deeds, and you should taste the bitterness of the hardship of obedience just as you tasted the sweetness of disobedience.

In linguistic analysis, the expected form would be to say: "He accepts repentance from His servants" (yaqbal al-tawbata min ʿibadihi). But the Truth says: ʿan ʿibadihi ("from His servants" with ʿan). It is as if the Truthful, glory be to Him, removes their sins from them when He accepts their repentance, so the result is the forgiveness of the sins they committed. However, the sins they committed have attributes from the Truth that demand their due from Him.

When the servant commits a sin, the attribute of al-Qahhar (the Subduer), al-Jabbar (the Compeller) and al-Muntaqim (the Avenger) comes into play, and these are attributes of majesty (jalal), which require punishment. Then come the attributes of beauty (jamal) from the Truth, glory be to Him: al-Ghafur (the Forgiving), al-Rahim (the Merciful), al-Tawwab (the Accepter of repentance)... etc.

So ﴿And He it is who accepts repentance from His servants﴾: He expressed it with ʿan ("from") although the repentance is from them, so that He might bear it on their behalf for them...

Meaning: Allah responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds. The verb "wa-yastajību" (and He responds) indicates swiftness of response, which is why it does not say "yujību." "Wa-yazīduhum min faḍlihi" (and He increases them from His bounty) also indicates that the response comes from Allah to them. In contrast: "Wal-kāfirūna lahum ʿadhābun shadīd" (as for the disbelievers, there is a severe punishment). The severe punishment of the disbelievers is the final destination, because the first thing they are met with is the wrath of Allah, then the veil, then the curse and expulsion from His mercy, then the punishment.

Then the Exalted says:

"Wa-law basaṭa Allāhu al-rizqa..." (And if Allah were to expand the provision...).

This verse establishes a characteristic of the human soul, as Allah says elsewhere: ﴿Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [Al-Alaq: 6-7]. When provision is spread out and made easy, a person is not preoccupied with it, nor with exertion for its sake. He does not toil or exhaust himself, and so he is free for other matters that occupy him, among them rebellion (al-baghy).

Therefore, when the Qur'an spoke of Qarun, who is the clearest example of tyrannical wealth, Allah said: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Moses, but he oppressed them﴾ [Al-Qasas: 76]. So, blessing and wealth may lead a person to tyranny and rebellion without right, and the expansion of provision means its abundance and the facilitation of its means. In this state, it is a form of trial.

As for His saying: ﴿But He sends down in a measured amount what He wills. Indeed He is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾ [Ash-Shura: 27], it means: He drives provision by a specific measure and with computation, according to the requirement of His knowledge and wisdom in managing the affairs of His creation. So He gives them in measured amounts, such that the servant does not reach the stage of tyranny and rebellion. He, glorified be He, is most knowing of the temperaments of His servants and most knowing of what sets them right. Therefore, there occurred in the sacred hadith (al-hadith al-qudsi, a saying of the Prophet in which Allah speaks in meaning):

And Islam has given great attention to the economic aspect of life's movement, and it enjoined zakat (obligatory almsgiving) in order to spread goodness throughout society. It taught us to distinguish between poverty resulting from incapacity and need, and poverty resulting from a trade and deception. Whoever makes poverty a trade has no share, and it is not right that you help him toward idleness and abstaining from work.

As for the incapable, he deserves it, because he is unable to earn. Therefore Allah has made for him a portion in the wealth of the capable that reaches him. He is honored and does not shed the water of his face for a morsel of food. Rather, the Truth, glorified be He, preserves his dignity, and makes you, O wealthy capable one, go to him, knock on his door, and give him, so that he knows that when Allah took away his capacity, He subjected to him the capacities of others.

Likewise, for example, in the obligation of hajj (the pilgrimage to Makkah), you see the one who is not able to perform it sad because he did not make the pilgrimage. In reality, he is more favored with Allah than the able one who makes the pilgrimage, because the able one may perform it and it may not be accepted from him, whereas the one who is not able has had the obligation dropped from him altogether. They say: ninety percent of people have not seen the House, meaning they have not circumambulated it. Does this mean that Allah deprives them of seeing it? No, rather they have a share of it, as it is said: "Among people is one who circumambulates the House, and among people is one whom the House circumambulates."

Then this state of poverty or incapacity does not last permanently among people, as Allah, glorified be He, says: ﴿And these days We alternate among the people﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 140].

We have already explained that poverty in society has a wisdom, because the movement of society and the interests of people cannot be sustained by mere bounty; rather, they are sustained by need. When need compels you, you work and do not disdain hard or lowly labor, for otherwise, who would perform these tasks?

We have seen that the worker, when he is content with Allah's decree concerning him and is sincere in his work, Allah says to him: "You were content with My decree, so I will give you according to My decree." Then you see him after a period has become an employer, after he was a hired worker, because he was sincere to his employer, did not harbor resentment toward him, and did not dislike the blessing that was with him.

So: the Truth, glorified be He, does not constrict provision, nor gives it in measure, except where there is a presumption of harm. Whoever Allah knows that expansion of provision would corrupt, He restricts the avenues of provision for him in order to set him right through poverty. The basic principle is that He, exalted be He, is generous and bountiful, expanding His provision for His servants. Therefore, He says in the following verse:

﴿And it is He who sends down...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 28:

﴿ٱلْغَيْثَ..﴾ [al-Shura: 28] The rain descends after a cessation and drought, so it gives relief to the people and rescues them from the drought, hunger and famine they are in. ﴿مِن بَعْدِ مَا قَنَطُواْ..﴾ [al-Shura: 28] "After they have despaired": they had despaired of its descent.

﴿وَيَنشُرُ رَحْمَتَهُ..﴾ [al-Shura: 28] "And He spreads His mercy": He extends it to all of His servants. ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلْوَلِيُّ..﴾ [al-Shura: 28] "And He is the Protector": the one who takes charge of the affairs of His servants and is benevolent towards them. ﴿ٱلْحَمِيدُ﴾ [al-Shura: 28] "The Praiseworthy": that is, the one praised for His blessings which He bestowed upon people and favoured them with. For He blessed you before He brought you into existence; He created for you the heavens and the earth, and subjected the whole universe to serve you. You arrived into a cosmos already prepared and ready to receive you, containing everything that sustains your life.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 29:

The word ﴿āyātihi...﴾ [al-Shura: 29]: its singular is āyah, which is a wondrous thing that calls you to reflection, as we say: so-and-so is an āyah (a sign, a marvel) in literature or in knowledge. We have said that the āyāt in the Noble Qur'an come with three meanings: cosmic signs that point to His power and the wondrous perfection of His making, such as the sun, the moon, the night and the day; miraculous signs that testify to the truthfulness of the messengers in conveying from God; and then the āyāt that carry rulings, which are the āyāt of the Noble Qur'an.

Here the Almighty and Exalted tells us about some of His cosmic signs: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾ [al-Shura: 29]. For they are a wondrous thing in creation, which points to God's power, His wisdom, and the all-encompassing scope of His power. And in another place He said: ﴿Certainly the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾ [Ghafir: 57].

Yes, greater. For man is born and dies: he dies as a child, he dies as a youth, indeed he dies in his mother's womb, and even if he lives a hundred years he will die. So where is the one who created the heavens and the earth, and what is in them of cosmic signs that populate whatever God wills?

So: man must remember these truths and say to himself: Is it reasonable that these signs should live longer than me while they are subjected to serve me? Then: I must have another life that befits my station, and with which God has favored me over these creatures. So: I have another life in which I will remain and abide when all these creatures perish.

His saying ﴿the heavens and the earth...﴾ [al-Shura: 29] means: and what is in them, because they are a container containing many creatures. Therefore He said in another place: ﴿To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 284].

The meaning of ﴿wa mā baththa...﴾ [al-Shura: 29], i.e., spread: ﴿in them of living creatures...﴾ [al-Shura: 29], i.e., in the heavens and in the earth. What crawls on the earth, i.e., what walks upon it, of humans and animals and birds; and what crawls in the sky is meant to refer to the angels.

﴿And He is, over their gathering when He wills...﴾ [al-Shura: 29], meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿All-Powerful﴾ [al-Shura: 29], i.e., able, as He said: ﴿the Day of Gathering, about which there is no doubt...﴾ [al-Shura: 7].

Some scholars held that there exist other creatures in the heights, who are like us, bearing obligations. In the solar system there are other worlds besides the earth, such as Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and others. The greatness lies in the gathering of all of them.

The word "muṣība" (calamity) is derived from iṣābat al-sahm lil-hadaf (the arrow striking its target). If the archer is skilled, he hits the target without deviation; so worldly calamities are like arrows already released, and they must strike their owners. Therefore they say: a calamity does not arise at the moment it occurs; rather it is decreed from eternity, and it is an arrow already shot, so its time is the distance the arrow travels to reach you, as we mentioned earlier regarding the calamity of death.

Thus it is a settled matter, a recorded and written decree from eternity, not something newly occurring. The whole universe has a "blueprint" (maket) in which everything is recorded and clarified. Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿No calamity befalls you on the earth or in yourselves except that it is in a Record before We bring it into being. Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾ [al-Hadid: 22]. So there is no escape at all from calamity, no way to flee from it, and it is never possible to guard against it, because the arrow that has been shot cannot be returned.

The calamities that befall a person are of two kinds: one in which you have a hand and a role, and one in which you have no role at all. For example, a student who fails at the end of the year because he neglected his lessons and did not strive has, without doubt, a role in this calamity that befell him at the end of the year. So if you do not want this calamity to strike you, then take the means of success, beware of the causes of failure, and you will find success.

The other: a calamity in which you have no role.
