Like a student who studies, strives and memorizes his lessons, but at the hour of the examination he is struck by dizziness or a sudden illness, so he cannot complete the examination and fails. This is an event by the decree of Allah, and the One who ordained the decree over him is his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and there is surely wisdom in it. Therefore it is obligatory to be content with this calamity as the decree and destiny of Allah, and a calamity becomes easier, however great it is, when the one afflicted believes that it is from Allah and not from anyone other than Him.

We have previously clarified this matter with an example from reality. We said: suppose you are sitting and your small son enters upon you with blood flowing from his face. The first thing that comes to your mind is to ask him: who did this to you? So you did not pass judgment on the event; rather you asked about its doer, because the event in itself does not grieve or gladden except through the agent who accompanies it.

If the boy says to you: "My uncle So-and-so hit me," you calm down, and you say to him: "You must have done something deserving punishment." But if he says: "Our neighbour So-and-so hit me," you become angry and turn the world upside down.

So: if the event comes from one who loves you, we accept it, know that behind it lies a benefit, and are content with it; and if it comes from an enemy, there is no benefit in it, and we object to it.

The Exalted wants to teach us how to receive calamities, and that every calamity comes with a cause. If we know it, we are at ease with it; if we are ignorant of it, we say: there must be wisdom of Allah in it, and we enter through the door of contentment and submission instead of entering through the door of wrath and objection.

So the student who suffered dizziness and did not sit the examination says to himself: perhaps I was conceited, so Allah wanted to eliminate my conceit; or perhaps I would have obtained a total lower than I wished; or perhaps Allah warded off through this the evil eyes of the envious.

Did the Exalted not say concerning His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes...﴾ [al-Qalam: 51].

The Exalted, in Surat al-Kahf, gives us an example and a model that teaches us how to receive events and how to accept calamities. So, since you have no role in them, there must be wisdom of Allah in them. Read the story of the righteous servant with our master Musa, peace be upon them both. The righteous servant was not a prophet, yet the Prophet learned from him and asked to accompany him. When the servant advances in his relationship with his Lord, Allah opens for him conquests from Himself and teaches him a knowledge He gives only to His elite.

The righteous servant was worshipping Allah on the method of our master Musa, yet Musa followed him to learn from him, because the mission of the Messenger is to bring the one he is sent to to his Lord; when he has brought him to his Lord, he leaves him to his own affairs with Allah, and then each servant has his own cleverness in his relationship with Allah, the Exalted. This righteous servant drew near to Allah and entered into a bond of affection with Him, so he had a special affair with Him.

Look at our master Musa saying to the righteous servant: ﴿Musa said to him, "May I follow you on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught of guidance?" He said, "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me"﴾ [al-Kahf: 66-67]. That is because you will see matters that do not please you and deeds whose wisdom you cannot grasp: ﴿And how can you have patience about that which you do not encompass in knowledge?" He said, "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter." He said, "If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you"﴾ [al-Kahf: 68-70].

Then the journey begins, and Musa sets out in the company of the righteous servant, and the first event between them was the ship: ﴿So they set out, until when they boarded the ship, he tore it open. [Musa] said, "Have you torn it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing."﴾ [al-Kahf: 71].

This was Musa's first objection, because the deed in its outward appearance is strange and deserves objection. ﴿He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?" [Musa] said, "Do not blame me for what I forgot and do not cover my affair with hardship."  So they set out until, when they met a boy, he killed him. [Musa] said, "Have you killed a pure soul for other than manslaughter? You have certainly done a terrible thing."﴾ [al-Kahf: 72-74]. Munkaran means: a denounced thing.

Yes, Musa could not be patient as he saw this strange deed which in his view was denounced: ﴿He said, "Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?" [Musa] said, "If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have been given an excuse from me." So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. And they found within it a wall about to collapse, so he set it upright. [Musa] said, "If you had wished, you could have taken for it a payment."﴾ [al-Kahf: 75-77].

This was the third, and the condition that Musa had imposed on himself was fulfilled, so the righteous servant decided to part from him. But before they parted he said to him: come, I will clarify for you what your patience did not bear regarding these events: ﴿He said, "This is parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you were unable to have patience. As for the ship, it belonged to needy people who worked on the sea, and I wanted to damage it because there was behind them a king who seizes every ship by force."﴾ [al-Kahf: 78-79]. That is: seizes every sound ship.

Undoubtedly, tearing the ship was an apparent calamity for its owners, but Allah the Exalted has wisdom in it, since behind these needy people there was an unjust king who seizes every good ship and usurps it, so I wanted to cause it a defect so that he would not take it.

So: here we are not comparing a torn ship with a sound ship; rather we are comparing a torn ship with there being no ship at all. Tearing the ship is easier for its owners than its being taken entirely, and afterwards they can repair it; the important thing is that it be saved for them from this king. ﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would impose upon them tyranny and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer to mercy﴾ [al-Kahf: 80-81]. So in Allah's knowledge he would be an undutiful son who would bring trial upon his parents, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them...﴾ [al-Taghabun: 14]. So there was wisdom in his being done away with.

If you say: what is the sin of the boy, that he be killed while small? They said: he has no sin, but there was in it a benefit and good that reaches him too, since he was taken while young; we spared him life, so he did not suffer in it and did not commit any of its misdeeds, and he died before the age of obligation, so he will not be held accountable for anything. Then he will be among the martyrs, and his dwelling is in Paradise, where he roams wherever he wishes and enters any place, even upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; he is among the (da'ami's) of Paradise. So his killing came as mercy towards him. ﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure for them. Their father had been righteous, so your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience﴾ [al-Kahf: 82].

First, we learned that this town had base people with no good in them, as evidenced by their refusing them food, and refusing food is baseness and vileness, because one who asks for food is not one who asks for money; one who asks you for money may hoard it, but asking for food is only out of need.

Therefore they said: the most truthful of those who ask you is one who asks you for food. So when they refused them food, it was a strange matter that the righteous servant should build them the wall. What is its story? The wall belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and imagine the condition of the two orphans among these miscreants, how it would be if this treasure had appeared to them.

From this matter we understood that the righteousness of parents benefits children, that the two boys were twins, as evidenced by His saying ﴿that they should reach their maturity...﴾ [al-Kahf: 82], for if one had been older than the other he might have taken it for himself; and that the righteous servant built the wall as a temporary construction, so that it would stand only until the two boys reached the age of puberty, and then it would collapse so they could find the treasure and be able to protect it from these miscreants. Furthermore, in building the wall there was a punishment for these miserly people and retribution against them for their stinginess, since he prevented them from taking the wealth of this treasure.

Finally, the righteous servant did not neglect to explain to our master Musa that what he had done was not from himself, but by a command from Allah: ﴿And I did not do it of my own accord﴾ [al-Kahf: 82]; rather it was by the command of Allah. So, when a calamity descends upon you and you have no role in it, then seek the wisdom in it, and you will surely find it and be guided to it.

As for the address in ﴿And whatever disaster strikes you is for what your hands have earned...﴾ [al-Shura: 30], it is an address to the general public, including believers and disbelievers. The disbeliever, because he entered the battle and was defeated, if his wealth is taken or he is killed, then it is because of his disbelief. As for the believer, he may have committed violations and sins that deserve punishment, as in the prescribed penalty for fornication and the prescribed penalty for drinking wine, for example, or that he be disciplined (ta'zir).

The Exalted sent revelation to His Messenger ﷺ that he should alert his community and teach them how to receive calamities, so the Messenger ﷺ said: [...]. Therefore one of the knowers said: "I truly know my standing with my Lord from the character of my mount," meaning: when his mount balks at him or stumbles, he asks himself: what have I done that the mount balks? Our mistress Asma', daughter of our master Abu Bakr, used to suffer from a persistent headache; she would hold her head and say: "It is for my sin, and Allah pardons much."

To clarify this matter we said: the Exalted created man and determined his mission in life, and set for him a method that protects him and regulates his movement in it. If he opposes this method, a defect must befall him, like a machine that a person makes, for which he sets a "catalogue" (manual) explaining how to use it; if these instructions are violated, the machine breaks down.

So the Exalted wants us to be mindful of this matter, so that the believer may be reassured when a calamity strikes him or a disaster descends upon him, so he is patient, does not despair, and does not protest, but seeks the wisdom or looks into himself: what have I done for this calamity to befall me? It will surely wash away from me something I committed and a sin I perpetrated.

This is the state of the sincere believer: to return to himself and hold himself to account, because he knows from what Allah has taught him that this world is an abode of action, not an abode of recompense; recompense is in the Hereafter: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned...﴾ [Ghafir: 17]. So what befalls me in this world of trials and calamities is not a recompense; rather it is a reminder to righteous action, and so that I learn from the materiality of things that transgression must have a punishment.

Then we see calamities befall the truthful and the heretic alike, and they encompass everyone, even the prophets. Therefore it is related in a hadith of our master the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: [...]. The trials of the prophets are not for sins they committed; rather they are a test in the duty of religious obligation and an example for others, an example that corrects the state of the people and teaches them patience at calamity. So when calamities descend upon us, we remember the calamities of the prophets, and how they were patient, so we are patient like them, and we correct our conduct towards Allah.

As for His saying: ﴿and He pardons much﴾ [al-Shura: 30], it means: much of our sins and transgressions; and were it not for His pardon and mercy towards His creation, no one would be saved.

Therefore we say to whoever is struck by a calamity: "Expiation, God willing" — meaning: Allah has made it an expiation for your sins. And it is related in the hadith qudsi: [...]. Yes, Allah lavishes good upon him in the abode of transience, because he has no share in the abode of permanence.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 31:

The Truth, glory be to Him, addresses the people who obstinately opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), clashed with his call and argued with him. He says to them: You will not escape the justice of the heavens, and whoever of you escapes the punishment of this world will not escape the punishment of the Hereafter, as He, glory be to Him, said addressing His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Whether We show you part of what We promise them, or We take you (in death), to Us they will be returned﴾ [Ghafir: 77].

Here He says to them: ﴿And you cannot escape (Allah) in the earth...﴾ [al-Shura: 31]. The mu'jiz (one who causes incapacity) is the one who attributes incapacity to me; a'jazani means he brings about a matter that I am not able to do. So the Truth says to them: You will not render Us incapable, and you will never flee from Us. Wherever you are, We will bring you.

Thus the cleverness of the jinn became clear to us when they said: ﴿And we thought that we could never escape Allah in the earth, nor could we escape Him by flight﴾ [al-Jinn: 12]. The jinn, who are more capable of fleeing than humans, nevertheless acknowledge that none of them can flee or escape from Allah, mighty and majestic is He.

Then, the Truth, glory be to Him, gives the wrongdoer respite and delays him, until when He seizes him He does not release him. That Allah, glory be to Him, grants these people respite does not mean He is incapable of seizing them, for He is powerful, capable, and possesses absolute power, such that He brings them whenever He wills. As for the weak, he seizes the first opportunity for revenge and does not let it pass, because he knows it will not return, as the poet said:

"A weak one, when he gets an opportunity, kills; such is the power of the weak."

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you have no protector or helper other than Allah﴾ [al-Shura: 31]. The wali (protector) is the relative or close friend who is always near you, and it is expected of him that he repels calamity from you before it befalls you. The nasir (helper) is the one who supports you and aids you when calamity has befallen you. Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, teaches us that the matter of responsibility (al-taklif) should be upright within us, that our connection with Allah should be direct, that we should not believe we can escape from Him, glory be to Him, and that we should not believe in any of His creation being a protector or helper for us.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 32:

Al-Jawari (the ships that run) in the sea is a description of a known thing, namely ships. They are the ones that run over the surface of the water. Today we see giant ships and steamships of great weight, which the water carries by God's permission, just as we find transport trucks and containers of great weight carried by air on wheels. These are among the signs of God, that the light should carry the heavy.

The meaning of ﴿like mountains﴾ [al-Shura: 32]: al-a'lam, its singular being 'alam, which is the mountain. It was called 'alam because of its height and prominence. Therefore al-Khansa', in lamenting her brother Sakhr, said:

"As if he were a mountain-landmark with fire on its summit."

So al-Khansa's saying about her brother, "As if he were a mountain-landmark with fire on its summit," is a metaphor (kinaya) that he was famous and known to everyone. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) heard this verse, he said: ...

And in this verse there is a manifestation of the signs of inimitability (i'jaz) and a sign for the Prophet (ﷺ). If we asked men of economics and industry: when did giant ships composed of several decks, resembling a mountain moving over the surface of the water, first appear? They would say: in the eighteenth century. So Muhammad did not see such ships. Who then informed him of this development? And who told him that they would be like mountains? It is God, who gives us the signs that attest to the truthfulness of His Prophet (ﷺ).

Moreover, the ships that run in the sea need energy to propel them. Where does this energy come from? When ships first began, they moved by the force of the wind or by the force of the water pushing them. If they were travelling in the same direction as the current, the current carried them along; and if they were travelling against the current, they used the wind to propel them by means of the sail. If the wind calms, they remain motionless on its surface.

So: they run by God's command and they stand still by God's command. And if they were travelling in a river and swimming against the current of the water, they would bring workers and ropes to haul the ship while they walk on the bank and move it along:

﴿If He wills, He calms the wind, so they remain motionless on its surface...﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 42, verse 33:

The meaning of ﴿فَيَظْلَلْنَ﴾ [al-Shura: 33] is: the ships. ﴿رَوَاكِدَ﴾ [al-Shura: 33] means fixed and still, not moving. The waves may stir them in their place, but they remain fixed and do not travel. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ﴾ [al-Shura: 33]: ﴿صَبَّارٍ﴾ is an intensive form (sigha mubalagha) of ṣābir (patient), the one who is very patient, because the movement of ships requires effort and hardship, so long patience is necessary.

Likewise ﴿شَكُورٍ﴾ [al-Shura: 33] is on the pattern fa'ūl, and it is also an intensive form of shākir (grateful). The movement of ships is among the signs of God that call for thanks for them.

Then this verse came after the words of God Most High ﴿وَمَآ أَصَـٰبَكُمْ مِّن مُّصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ [al-Shura: 30]. Calamities too require the one who is very patient and very grateful, because when a misfortune befalls a person, it does not strike all his limbs nor consume all of him. God afflicts you in one thing and grants you well-being in others. The afflicted person needs patience, and the one who is spared needs gratitude.

For this reason it is narrated that our master ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar, when he went to al-Shām, had his leg injured on the road, and he found no one to treat him because of the length of the journey. It festered, became infected, and gangrene set in. When he reached Damascus and stayed as a guest of the caliph, physicians were brought to him. They decided to amputate it and sought for him a muraqqad, which is like anaesthetic today, so that he would not feel the pain. But he refused and said: "By God, I do not wish to be heedless of my Lord for the blink of an eye." Indeed they cut off his leg without warning, because one who enjoys this companionship and feels this feeling is worthy of not feeling pain while in the companionship of God.

This is the companionship in which our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and his companion took refuge in the cave, when he said to him: "Do not grieve, indeed God is with us." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of God, if one of them looked beneath his feet he would see us." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "That is because they are in the companionship of God, and God is not perceived by sight." Likewise, whoever is in the companionship of God, God grants him a share of this quality.

So when our master ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar said: "I do not wish to be heedless of my Lord for the blink of an eye," they cut off his leg while he was in this state, and he did not feel its pain. When they wanted to bury it, he took hold of it and said: "O God, if You tested me in one limb, You have granted well-being to (many) limbs." Thus this is an example of the servant who is patient and grateful: patient in calamity, grateful for blessing.

In His saying, glorified be He: ﴿إِن يَشَأْ يُسْكِنِ ٱلرِّيحَ﴾ [al-Shura: 33] there is another aspect of Qur'anic miraculousness. In former times the ship moved only by the wind, but now it moves by the power of fuel or electricity and does not need the wind. Does the ships' independence from the wind mean that the verse no longer has application? They say: No, rather it is enduring and everlasting, and it has a meaning that holds until the Hour, because among the meanings of the word "wind" (rīḥ) is strength, whatever it may be.

Read, if you wish, His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَنَازَعُواْ فَتَفْشَلُواْ وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ﴾ [al-Anfal: 46], that is: your strength. So if you have become independent of the wind, the meaning of strength remains, whether it is by steam or otherwise.

His saying ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ﴾ [al-Shura: 33], following ﴿فَيَظْلَلْنَ رَوَاكِدَ عَلَىٰ ظَهْرِهِ﴾ [al-Shura: 33], is an indication to the owners of ships and their passengers that if they stop moving because the wind has died down, they should not grieve. They should meet this matter with some patience, and thank God that the hardship came in this form and was not more than that, such as the ship suffering damage, a storm, or other calamities. That is: be patient over what you have lost, and be grateful for what remains to you.

Meaning of ﴿yubqihinna..﴾ [al-Shura: 34]: that is, either they (the ships) remain still upon its surface, or He drowns them ﴿bima kasabu..﴾ [al-Shura: 34]: because of what they did of disobedience, such as drinking wine, gambling and other things; ﴿wa-ya'fu 'an kathir﴾ [al-Shura: 34]: that is, He pardons much of their sins, so He does not take them to account for them.

In another place, the Exalted One explains this matter: ﴿He it is who enables you to travel on land and sea, until when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it, there comes upon them a violent wind and the waves come at them from everywhere, and they think they are encompassed. They call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion: "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful." But when He saves them, at once they commit injustice upon the earth without right...﴾ [Yunus: 22-23].

Meaning: they have no refuge and no escape from the punishment of Allah. Those who dispute with the Messenger of Allah concerning the signs of Allah and deny him know Allah's power over them, and that if He wills, He will seize them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Able.

And "حاص" (ḥāṣa) in place means: he went here or there and finds no rest. In our colloquial expression there is something that depicts this, when we say "فلان حايص" (fulan ḥāyiṣ), meaning: he cannot find a place in which to rest, and he does not know where to go, so there is no escape and no way of deliverance.

Commentary on the words of Allah: "Whatever you have been given of anything" (42:36)

His saying: ﴿of anything﴾ [al-Shura: 36] means: everything that can be called a thing (shay') of the enjoyments of life, such as wealth, children, wives, positions, health, status, and so on. All of this is merely the enjoyment of the worldly life, which you enjoy in this world. The world, with respect to you, is not the period from Adam until the Hour arises; rather, it is the duration of your own stay in it, with which the lifespans of others have nothing to do. You do not pass through the world; rather, the world passes through you.

Therefore: however great your enjoyment is, it is limited by your lifespan in this world, and it comes to an end, ﴿But what is with Allah is better and more enduring, for those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾ [al-Shura: 36]. This is because in this world you enjoy in proportion to your effort in it and in proportion to your capabilities, whereas in the Hereafter the enjoyment is in proportion to the Truth, glory be to Him. And although the enjoyment of this world passes away, the enjoyment of the Hereafter remains, lasting and eternal.

Therefore: when you measure the level of blessing you live in this world against the level of blessing in the Hereafter, you will know that what is with Allah is better and more enduring. And when you come to know this truth, you must work for it, because this superiority and this permanence are conditional upon "those who believe and upon their Lord they rely." So here there is both creed and action through the means (asbab).

There is also a distinction between one who relies upon Allah (tawakkul) by first taking the means and then relying upon Allah, and one who is reliant on others without effort (tawakkul in the sense of tawakkul, i.e., "tawakkul" as neglect), who says "I have relied upon Allah" and abandons striving and taking the means. Therefore: the believer relies upon Allah with his heart and works with his limbs.

This verse, ﴿So whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of the worldly life...﴾ [al-Shura: 36], was revealed concerning a group of the leaders of Quraysh, at their head al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, when they envied the Messenger of Allah and harbored resentment against him because Allah had chosen him for prophethood. They said: ﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31], meaning: he has such-and-such. So Allah answered them that all of this is worldly enjoyment that passes away, and what is with Allah is better than it and more enduring.

The meaning of "yajtanibun" (they shun/avoid): that is, they keep away from the things that lead to the major sins and the grave immoralities. The kaba'ir (major sins) are the great transgressions for which Allah has threatened the one who commits them and prescribed a punishment. The fawahish (grave immoralities) are everything whose ugliness and indecency is great. All of these are sins that necessitate the application of the hadd (prescribed punishment) upon the one who commits them.

We have already said that the successive messages of the various messengers agreed on the prohibition of these major sins, and they urged the inner faculties to disassociate themselves from their defects. The heart disassociates itself from shirk and from persisting in disobedience, and it must not feel secure from the plotting of Allah, nor despair of the mercy of Allah.

The tongue disassociates itself from false testimony, from speaking falsehood, from slandering chaste women, and from the yamin ghamus (the perjurious oath) which plunges its swearer into the Fire. It is swearing falsely about something that has already happened in the past. This oath has no expiation (kaffarah). However, if one swears about something in the future and then something better becomes apparent to him, Allah permits him to do the better thing and to expiate his oath.

Likewise, the belly disassociates itself from drinking wine, from consuming the wealth of orphans, and from consuming riba (usury). The private parts disassociate themselves from every unlawful intercourse, the hand disassociates itself from theft and killing, and the foot disassociates itself from fleeing on the day of battle (al-zahf). Above all of this, all these limbs disassociate themselves from disobedience to the parents.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when they are angered, they forgive﴾. Anger (al-ghadab) is the boiling over of the instinct of anger at something that angered or troubled you, and this thing arose from a person, so there arises in you a desire for revenge or feelings of spite and envy toward him.

So the Almighty teaches us how to forgive, pardon, and overlook. If you love to be forgiven, then forgive the one who wronged you. When we reflect on the conditions of people, we observe that the outcome of pardon and forgiveness is praiseworthy, and the outcome of oppression and vengeance is disastrous.

Therefore, the Almighty guides us to take the path of pardon, to beware of the surge of anger, not to be carried away by it, and not to transgress the limits when this surge seizes us, even in the matter of retaliation (qisas): ﴿Retaliation is prescribed for you regarding the slain﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178].

After legislating qisas for us, it reminds us of what is more fitting and more guiding for us, which is pardon: ﴿But whoever is pardoned by his brother in any respect, then compliance in a fair manner and payment to him with good conduct﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178]. Thus qisas was legislated to preserve the right of its owner, then the door of pardon was opened.

Therefore, we find that the religion prohibits any person from interceding in a hadd of the limits of Allah, except in the case of killing, where intercession is permitted, because when the guardian of the one killed pardons the killer, he spreads affection in the society, and the killer becomes indebted to him, since he knows that his soul is held in pledge by this pardon.

And read the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better, and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune﴾ [Fussilat: 34-35].

This is a truth affirmed by the Creator, Exalted is He, who is most knowing of His servants. Therefore, we find some people on this matter saying to you: "By Allah, I repelled with what is better, but to no avail." We say to him: You must examine yourself and the extent of your sincerity in your conduct. You think you have repelled with what is better, but the reality is otherwise. You are testing Allah, and testing Allah is doubt. Had you been sincere, the verse would have been sincere with you...

Then reflect on why the verse emphasized the subject in ﴿yaghfirun﴾ by mentioning the detached pronoun (hum). He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And when they are angered, they forgive﴾. He said: "hum" to affirm that they are the people of decision; the forgiveness comes from them themselves, not as a courtesy to anyone, nor under compulsion from anyone. For you may send to the one who holds the right someone to intercede for you with him, and then when the rightful owner forgives, the favor is credited to the intercessor. So why, then, would you deprive yourself of the reward? Why not make it purely yours?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 38:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And those who have responded to their Lord﴾ [al-Shura: 38], meaning: by faith. This represents the creed. ﴿And establish prayer, and their affair is [determined by] consultation among themselves, and from what We have provided them, they spend﴾ [al-Shura: 38]: this represents action and application.

This is one of many verses that link prayer with zakat (obligatory charity), because through them the condition of the believing society is set right. Zakat is a relinquishing of part of your wealth to those in need, so in it you sacrifice wealth. Likewise, in prayer there is a purification more eloquent than the purification of wealth, because in prayer you sacrifice time, which is the sphere of work and the cause of earning wealth.

What is new in this verse, regarding the combining of prayer and zakat, is the mention of consultation (shura) between them. The one who speaks of this is the Truthful One, glory be to Him, so we must pause here and seek out the wisdom: why did He place consultation between these two matters which have always been brought together in the verses of the Wise Reminder?

We say: the meaning of (they establish prayer) is that they perform it in its most complete form, and this occurs in congregation in the mosque. So it is as if He seizes the opportunity of this gathering and commands them that their affair be by consultation among them. Consultation does not apply to a matter that Allah has enjoined upon us, nor to a matter that His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has enjoined upon us. Rather, it applies to matters of difference in which no text has come, so the ruling in them is by consultation among the people of specialization, as we see in the matter of fatwa (legal opinion).

For this reason we call for fatwa to be collective, not individual. When the group discusses, they must arrive at the correct view, and there is no harm in your defending the opinion of the group even if you have a differing opinion.

Then reflect on ﴿and their affair is [determined by] consultation among themselves..﴾ [al-Shura: 38]. He did not say "they consult" (tashawur). Rather, He expressed it with the verbal noun (masdar) to emphasize that their affair is itself consultation, as you say: "a just man" (rajul 'adl) and "a man of justice" (rajul 'adl, with the verbal noun), making him justice itself. It has been reported that Imam 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "O Messenger of Allah, matters come upon us for which we see no ruling from Allah, and we see no ruling in the Sunnah of His Prophet concerning them, so what should we do?" The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Gather the worshippers and make it a matter of consultation, and do not follow the opinion of a single person."

Meaning of ﴿when wrong afflicts them﴾ [al-Shura: 39]: they are struck by oppression and aggression. Al-baghy (transgression) means exceeding the limit in wrongdoing. ﴿they defend themselves﴾ [al-Shura: 39], i.e., they take retribution against the wrongdoer by the same measure, without exceeding it. This verse establishes a ruling of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, namely the permissibility of retaliating against the wrongdoer. However, the matter does not end at this ruling; rather, the Glorified One follows it with another ruling to complete the picture, so He says in the following verse:

﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it...﴾.

The Almighty Allah is merciful to His servants and gentle with them. When He permitted them to respond in kind in retaliation (qisas) and in cases of wrongdoing, He willed to satisfy the feelings and emotions of the wronged person and to relieve him by avenging himself on his oppressor. But He narrowed this door and widened the door of pardon, encouraging it. He narrowed the door of revenge for you when He said: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you endure patiently, it is better for those who are patient.﴾ [al-Nahl: 126].

So when the Almighty said ﴿The recompense for an evil is an evil like it...﴾ [al-Shura: 40], it was only to relieve your heart and to end enmity and hatred between the two parties. But when you take revenge, can you guarantee that you will respond with the like? Equivalence here is extremely difficult, and no one can achieve it. Take the simplest matter: if a person strikes another with a blow, or slaps him on the face, can he return the same blow without adding to it? If he adds to it, he too would be an oppressor. Thus, in pardon there is breadth and a way out of this difficulty and this constriction.

For this reason it is related that in Italy there was a usurer who lent a man money for a term, but stipulated that if he did not pay by the appointed date between them, he would cut off a pound of his flesh in exchange for this debt. When the date came and the debtor did not pay what he owed, the creditor brought his case before the judge. The judge upheld his condition and said to him: "You have the right to take a pound of his flesh, but remember: if you take more, we will take the excess from your own flesh, and if you take less, we will make up the shortfall from your own flesh." The usurer had no choice but to retract his condition.

For this reason the Most High says: ﴿So whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah. Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Shura: 40]. It is as if revenge must inevitably draw its doer into the realm of wrongdoing.

And on the authority of Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: And you may contemplate how the Creator reforms creation through these values, and it is incumbent upon us only to bring them out from the realm of theory into application and practice.

The "evil" (sayyi'ah) in His words ﴿The recompense for an evil is an evil like it...﴾ [al-Shura: 40] means: an action in which there is harm done to you by speech or deed, and it does not mean the evil of sins and disobediences against the right of Allah, the Most High.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 42, verses 41–42:

Allah's words ﴿And whoever defends himself after being wronged...﴾ [al-Shura: 41]. That is: whoever takes retribution against his oppressor. ﴿Those, there is no blame upon them﴾ [al-Shura: 41]. That is: there is no censure against them, because they did not exceed the limits of defending oneself and avenging oneself. ﴿The blame is only upon those who wrong the people and transgress upon the earth without right; those will have a painful punishment﴾ [al-Shura: 42]. (Al-sabil, "the way" or "the blame".) The meaning is: the way of censure. ﴿Upon those who wrong people and transgress upon the earth without right. Those will have a painful punishment﴾ [al-Shura: 42].

Then the Truth, glorified is He, takes the hands of His servants toward a path that is safer than retribution and more praiseworthy in its outcome, so He says, exalted is He:

﴿And whoever is patient and forgives...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 42, verses 41–42:

Allah's words ﴿And whoever defends himself after being wronged...﴾ [al-Shura: 41]. That is: whoever takes retribution against his oppressor. ﴿Those, there is no blame upon them﴾ [al-Shura: 41]. That is: there is no censure against them, because they did not exceed the limits of defending oneself and avenging oneself. ﴿The blame is only upon those who wrong the people and transgress upon the earth without right; those will have a painful punishment﴾ [al-Shura: 42]. (Al-sabil, "the way" or "the blame".) The meaning is: the way of censure. ﴿Upon those who wrong people and transgress upon the earth without right. Those will have a painful punishment﴾ [al-Shura: 42].
