﴿And whoever is patient and forgives...﴾.

The Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 43:

It is related in the counsel of Luqman to his son: ﴿And be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [Luqman: 17], without emphasis by the lam that appears here: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [al-Shura: 43].

It is true that the general meaning is one, namely the call to patience, but there is a difference between patience over a calamity in which you have no adversary (gharim), and patience over a calamity in which you have an adversary. The presence of an adversary requires strength in patience and endurance, because whenever you see your adversary, the motives for revenge stir within you. Luqman is advising his son to be patient over a calamity in which there is no adversary, so no emphasis was needed.

As for here, the discussion concerns patience when you have an adversary whom you are considering avenging, returning evil with its like. You are then in need of a strength that helps you to be patient, and a capacity that takes you from the domain of defending the self to the domain of pardon and forgiveness. Therefore the statement is emphasised with the lam twice in the verse.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives...﴾ [al-Shura: 43] means that we are before two stages: patience over wrongdoing, then forgiving the wrongdoing. Many people are patient with one who has wronged them, but do not forgive his wrong, because the stage of forgiveness requires strength of faith and strength of resolve. ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [al-Shura: 43].

That is: the important matters that require from you resolve, steadfastness, and a strength by which you extinguish the fire of rancour, vengeance and retaliation, and another strength from which you draw the capacity for forgiveness. This is not found except in the believer who is certain that what is with Allah is better and more lasting, and that he will gain by pardon what he would not gain by retaliation.

Therefore: the Exalted has permitted you to avenge yourself, then called you to pardon and encouraged you to it. So when is retaliation, and when is pardon? They said: pardon is better than retaliation and defending the self, except when the wrongdoer is one of the ignorant, whom pardon only increases in transgression, and whose forbearance towards him only increases his covetousness towards you. For such a person there must be dealing in kind, so that he may be restrained and not persist in wronging people.

Many of the early Arab poets were alert to this truth. Al-Mutanabbi says:

*Of forbearance is that you employ ignorance towards it,*
*when the paths of wrongdoing widen in forbearance.*

And he also said:

*If you honour the noble, you possess him,*
*and if you honour the base, he becomes defiant.*

*Placing generosity in the place of the sword in matters of exaltedness*
*is as harmful as placing the sword in the place of generosity.*

Another said:

*There is no good in forbearance when it has no*
*sudden flashes (bawadir) that protect its purity from being clouded.*

In the history of the Arab tribes there is what confirms this. Some tribes were fierce and strong and did not accept injustice, such as Banu Mazin. They were a proof (hujja) in defending themselves, so people feared them, and no one dared to transgress against them. Among the tribes that were ignorant and deceived by the pardon of those who pardoned them was the tribe of Banu al-Luqaytah of Banu Dhuhl.

As for Tayy, it was a peaceable tribe that pardoned, forgave, and returned evil with good. Therefore Banu Dhuhl coveted them and persisted in transgressing against them, until their poet overflowed (with anger) after they had violated his land and taken his camels. He was distressed by what his tribe had of pardon towards one who did not deserve pardon, and he said describing them:

*As if your Lord had not created for His fear*
*anyone among all of mankind other than them as human.*

*They repay the injustice of the unjust with forgiveness,*
*and the evil of the evil with goodness.*

Then he recited his famous ode in Arabic literature:

*We forgave Banu Dhuhl,*
*and we said: the people are brothers.*

*Perhaps the days will return them*
*to a people like those they were.*

*But when evil became manifest and it came to be naked,*
*we walked the gait of the lion in the morning, while the lion was angry,*

*with a blow that contains weakening, debilitation and subjugation,*
*and a thrust like the mouth of the waterskin, in the morning, while the skin is full.*

*And some forbearance in the presence of ignorance is submission to humiliation,*
*and in evil there is salvation at a time when goodness does not save you.*

How beautiful is the saying of the Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him:

*Even if I am in need of forbearance,*
*I am, at certain times, more in need of ignorance.*

*I have a horse for forbearance, bridled with forbearance,*
*and I have a horse for ignorance, saddled with ignorance.*

*So whoever seeks to straighten me, I am straight,*
*and whoever seeks to bend me, I am bent.*

Allah's statement, ﴿And whomever Allah sends astray...﴾ [ash-Shura: 44], means: Allah decrees for him misguidance, because guidance belongs to Allah. He, glory be to Him, has made clear to people the path of good and the path of evil, by guiding to good and forbidding evil.

This guidance, which we call the guidance of indication and direction (hidayat al-dalalah wal-irshad), Allah the Truthful has made available to both the believer and the disbeliever. Allah has indicated it to all of them. The believer accepted this guidance, acted by what it contains, and walked upon its way in what is commanded and in what is forbidden, so Allah increased him in guidance. As for the disbeliever, he ignored this guidance and did not act by it, so Allah increased him in the misguidance he had chosen for himself. Whoever desires something and loves it, Allah increases him in it, whether he is a believer or a disbeliever. Therefore He said of the believers: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their God-consciousness﴾ [Muhammad: 17]. As for the disbeliever, He has sealed his heart so that his disbelief does not leave it and the light of faith does not enter it.

As for His statement, ﴿So there is no protector for him...﴾ [ash-Shura: 44], meaning: no one who would befriend and support him, ﴿besides Him...﴾ [ash-Shura: 44], meaning: besides Allah, the Exalted. ﴿And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying: "Is there any way of return?"﴾ [ash-Shura: 44], meaning: Is there any path back to the world once more, so that we may repent and do righteous deeds? This is the question of one who is helpless and has no recourse. And what recourse do they have for returning, now that they have witnessed the punishment which they long denied and disbelieved in during the world?

Allah the Truthful refutes this claim of theirs. In another verse He says, addressing our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿If you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire and they say, "Oh, I wish we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers." Rather, there has become apparent to them what they had concealed before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'am: 27-28].

In another place, He, glory be to Him, said in response to them: ﴿Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteousness in what I have left behind." No! It is only a word he is saying, and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 99-100].

"His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And you will see them﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿being exposed to it﴾, to the Fire, ﴿humbled by abasement﴾, i.e., submissive and humiliated from intense fear. Therefore ﴿they look with a furtive glance﴾ [al-Shura: 45], meaning they steal glances and cannot face it with their eyes, for the disgrace they are in breaks their eyes.

Therefore you say to your opponent who slanders you falsely, "Bring your eye to my eye." Why? Because facing one another with the eyes reveals the truth. The person of truth has a strong, bold eye, drawing its strength from the strength of the truth he defends, whereas the eye of the falsifier is broken and humbled, shrinking from the ray of truth that exposes his falsehood.

﴿And those who believed will say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in lasting torment﴾ [al-Shura: 45]. This statement is repeated by the believer who has been saved from punishment and attained Paradise. He says: the true loss is what these people are in, for they have lost everything. ﴿Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in lasting torment﴾ [al-Shura: 45], meaning: enduring and unceasing."

The discussion here concerns the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And they will have no allies to help them against God﴾ [al-Shura: 46], meaning they will not be able to ward off the punishment that has come down upon them. ﴿And whomever God sends astray, for him there is no way﴾ [al-Shura: 46], meaning he has no path to guidance, because it is God, exalted is He, who guides. He sets the model for guidance.

We have already explained that guidance is of two kinds: the guidance of indication and direction (hidayat al-dalala wal-irshad), and the guidance of divine success and assistance (hidayat al-tawfiq wal-ma'una). For this reason we have seen some orientalists (al-mustashriqun, Western scholars of Islam) stand before certain verses and accuse the Qur'an of contradiction, such as His saying: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ [al-Qasas: 56], and in another place: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura: 52].

He affirmed guidance once and negated it another time, and the address here is to our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ). These people's objection to the style of the Qur'an results from their failure to understand the speech of God. The negation and the affirmation here are both valid because the aspect is distinct: the object of the affirmation of guidance has one meaning, and the object of its negation has another meaning.

We have also explained that guidance is of two types: guidance of indication and direction, and guidance of assistance and success. The Messenger of God possesses the guidance of indication and direction, but does not possess the guidance of success and assistance. The latter is in the hand of God alone; He guides to Himself whomever He wills.

So His saying: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ [al-Qasas: 56] negates from him the guidance of success and assistance, because it belongs to God, exalted is He. And His saying: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura: 52] affirms for him the guidance of indication and direction. Therefore, the aspect is distinct and there is no contradiction between the two passages.

Consider also His saying, addressing His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was God who threw﴾ [al-Anfal: 17]. In the matter of the act, He negated it and affirmed it in one passage, because the aspect is likewise distinct, and each of the two acts has its own meaning.

Likewise in His saying: ﴿God does not break His promise, but most of the people do not know. They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, while they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾ [al-Rum: 6-7], meaning: they do not know the realities of things; they only know their outward appearance.

In our daily lives we use this style of negating and affirming an act in a single statement. When you see your son opening a book and looking at its lines while his mind is elsewhere, or when you ask him after study and he does not answer, you say to him: "You studied, and yet you did not study," meaning: you studied the form but did not study the subject or its content.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Respond to your Lord...﴾.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Respond to your Lord...﴾

Here is a command to respond to an order from whom? To the order of the Lord, ﴿your Lord﴾. The Lord is the One who created you from nothing and sustained you from non-existence, took charge of your upbringing and care, and bestowed favour upon you. He, glorified is He, is the Owner of the method, the Master of the recompense, and capable of it; to Him alone is the return and the final abode. Therefore He is worthy of being responded to when He commands, and most deserving of obedience. The intelligent person is the one who hastens to respond to God, exalted is He.

We note here that the Qur'an used the word al-istijabah (response that is sought, i.e., answering with acceptance and compliance), rather than al-ijabah (a simple answer), because al-istijabah is a branch of seeking (talab). Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And Allah responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Shura: 26], meaning: Allah responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds.

So when the Truth, glorified is He, calls you and invites you to prayer, for example, you must answer the call, because He has invited you for your own benefit. He invites you to give you a charge of faith through your presence in the company of Allah. The call of Allah akbar means: come, hayya 'ala al-salah (come to prayer), hayya 'ala al-falah (come to success), come and meet Me.

The Lord, glorified is He, is the One who invites you to meet Him, and welcomes you into His house and His company in order to set them right. If they do not respond, they are sinful, guilty, disobedient, and deserving of punishment, while the Truth, glorified is He, gains nothing from that.

If we draw a comparison between meeting the Truth, glorified is He, and meeting a president or an official, the difference would be clear. You are the one who requests the meeting; even if it is granted to you, the appointment, the subject of discussion, the place of the meeting and its end are all set by others, and you own none of its elements.

As for your meeting with your Lord, mighty and majestic is He, He is the One who invites you into His presence not once but five times a day and night, and opens the door for you to say whatever you want, and you end the meeting whenever you wish.

In the meeting He grants you a charge of faith that helps you in the affairs of your religion and your worldly life, sets right what has been corrupted in your soul or your thoughts, forgives your minor sins, expands your breast, and your heart finds tranquility through it.

Someone may ask: how does all this happen to me?

We say: Allah, glorified is He, is unseen (ghayb), so when He sets you right, He sets you right by His unseen power, and when He gives you by His unseen power, from where you do not perceive and do not expect. Therefore, our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when a matter distressed him, would stand in prayer.

He (ﷺ) used to say about the prayer: "Give us rest by it, O Bilal." You too should follow his example: when the means become narrow for you, and when worry or grief befalls you, hasten to prayer.

It is natural that the response to His command, exalted is He, be restricted to the life of this world, for it is the field of action. Therefore He said: ﴿before there comes a Day from Allah which cannot be turned back﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection, which no one can repel and which none can delay from its time.

﴿You will have no refuge that Day﴾, meaning: you will have no place to seek refuge in which would protect you from the punishment; ﴿nor will you have any denial﴾, meaning: none who will deny your punishment or oppose it and object to it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 42, verse 48:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away﴾ [al-Shura: 48], i.e., from all these matters, and abandon you and turn away from the method with which you came to them. And of the same kind is His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿And when We bestow favour upon man, he turns away and withdraws to one side﴾ [al-Isra: 83]. So if they turn away from you, O Muhammad, ﴿We have not sent you as a guardian over them. Your duty is only to convey (the message)﴾ [al-Shura: 48].

This is a consolation for our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because he was always eager for the guidance of the people, and their turning away and withdrawal from the guidance he brought grieved him. He would strain himself over this matter until he nearly destroyed himself. Therefore his Lord addressed him in more than one place, consoling him, easing his burden, and forbidding him to burden himself beyond his capacity.

He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 3]. And He said in al-Kahf: ﴿Then perhaps you would destroy yourself following them, out of grief, if they do not believe in this message﴾ [al-Kahf: 6].

And here He says to him: ﴿We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾ [al-Shura: 48], meaning: a watcher over them, (to see) who believes and who disbelieves. So your task, O Muhammad, is merely conveyance, ﴿Your duty is only to convey﴾ [al-Shura: 48], and it is not for you to compel anyone to believe.

Then the Truth, Glorified is He, establishes a reality upon which man has been created: ﴿And when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it...﴾ [al-Shura: 48]. It is a logical matter that man rejoices in mercy and in good that is brought to him, and "rejoicing" here means exultation (al-batar), and "man" here is a generic noun (ism jins) denoting generality.

﴿But if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, then indeed man is ungrateful﴾ [al-Shura: 48]. Note that mercy is not attributed to man, because it is not the work of his hand; rather, evil is attributed to him because it is the result of his striving and the fruit of his hands.

So: evil is not attributed to Allah, because it is by your own deed. If you attribute it to Allah, you have disbelieved in Him. ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful﴾ [al-Shura: 48]: ungrateful for the favour of Allah upon him. And among ingratitude for favour is to attribute causes to other than the Causer.

Ingratitude for favour and denial of it is a natural disposition in man, except for those whom Allah has mercied. For example, a man comes knocking at your door asking you to intercede for him in some matter, so you stand by his side and help him until he accomplishes his need. The reality is that Allah is the One who decides and facilitates, and you are only a means, and your intervention coincided with the time of its fulfilment. That is to say: it would have been fulfilled without an intermediary.

So: your intercession did not bring the benefit to the other; rather it coincided with acceptance. The strange thing thereafter is that you find a man arrogant, who does not acknowledge the kindness of his benefactor and attributes it to himself: "I did such-and-such, and I was ready for such-and-such." Why? Because kindness is a benefaction, and benefaction makes you humbled before the one who did it to you.

Do good to people and you will enslave their hearts; for man has long been enslaved by kindness.

Thus the one who denies a kindness wants to free himself from this humiliation. The denier of kindness is much like Qarun, who said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge that I have﴾ [al-Qasas: 78]. And it was said long ago: beware the evil of the one to whom you have done good. Why? Because you remind him of his state of weakness and his need for help.

So: ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful﴾ [al-Shura: 48], i.e., toward favour: he loves to attribute it to himself, and at the same time he distances from himself evil and misfortune. Both are ingratitude for the favour of Allah.

When the Truth, Glorified is He, speaks to us of His favour, He says: ﴿And if you should count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾ [Ibrahim: 34]. Firstly: the use of (in, "if"), which denotes doubt, because the favours of Allah are so numerous that they cannot be counted, and no one ventures to count them, since you only proceed to counting something that is likely to be enumerable. No one says, for example: count the grains of sand.

Likewise, the favours of Allah exceed the possibility of counting and enumeration. Then He used the word ﴿favour﴾ [Ibrahim: 34] in singular form and did not say "favours." A single favour cannot be counted, so what of favours?

This verse ﴿And if you should count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾ [Ibrahim: 34] came with this wording in two places in the Book of Allah. One was concluded with His saying: ﴿Indeed, man is most unjust and ungrateful﴾ [Ibrahim: 34], and the other with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nahl: 18].

The difference in the concluding phrases of the two verses has meaning, because the matter of favour has elements: a Bestower, who is Allah, Mighty and Majestic; a bestowed upon, who is the servant; and then the favour itself, which cannot be counted or enumerated.

The attribute of the Bestower, Glorified is He, is that He is Generous, giving His servant and bestowing upon him even if he denies the favour or disbelieves in it. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nahl: 18]. And the attribute of the one bestowed upon is that he denies the favour and disbelieves in it, out of wrongdoing and transgression. Therefore He said in the other: ﴿Indeed, man is most unjust and ungrateful﴾ [Ibrahim: 34].

Al-Sha'rawi, commentary on Surah 42, verse 49:

The Exalted Lord speaks here of His ownership of the heavens and the earth as a receptacle for things, and at the beginning of the surah He spoke of His ownership of what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, saying: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and He is the Most High, the Mighty﴾ [al-Shura: 4].

So: to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and this style

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth﴾ [al-Shura: 4] and ﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth…﴾ [al-Shura: 49]

is called the style of restriction (qasr), in which the prepositional phrase (al-jar wa al-majrur) is placed before the subject (al-mubtada') to convey restriction. The meaning is: to God alone belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, restricted to Him, and to God alone belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Ownership here has no partner and no contender.

The root (m-l-k) is pronounced with the mim in three ways: with a fatha, a damma and a kasra. The word mulk (with a kasra) is everything that is in your possession and that you dispose of; with a damma it is the disposal of the property of one who owns, and this is the familiar usage in the system of a kingdom (mamlakah); and with a fatha, as in His saying: ﴿We did not break our promise to you by our own choice﴾ [Ta-Ha: 87], meaning: against our will and without our intention.

As for the letter lam in malk, it also comes with a kasra as milk, which is one who is made to own in another's domain, in his disposal and his will; and with a fatha as malak, which is the highest of created beings among the angels. And "milak al-amr" means its essence and its reality.

His saying, "To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth" [al-Shura: 49], means: He is their owner, their creator and their originator, because you may own what you do not make.

﴿He creates what He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 49] means: He creates it according to His will and His volition, and He has absolute power in the matter of creation; nothing overcomes Him in it and no matter eludes Him.

Therefore, He gives us the evidence for this from the reality of our lives that we observe in society, which everyone knows. Read: ﴿He grants to whom He wills daughters, and He grants to whom He wills sons, or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes barren whom He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 49-50]. First, note that this matter is a gift from God the Creator, glory be to Him: ﴿He grants to whom He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 49], meaning it is not a right of anyone, nor a right of everyone who possesses its causes. A married life may be complete and yet no fruit of childbearing comes, and the spouses are tried with barrenness, which is also a gift from God.

Whoever is content with this gift and believes that it is from God, God compensates him, and he sees in the children of others a kindness that parents do not see, and he enjoys this kindness without the toil and hardship of raising these children. In our reality, a son may come who is undutiful to his parents.

Then you notice that the Exalted Lord placed females before males: ﴿He grants to whom He wills daughters, and He grants to whom He wills sons﴾ [al-Shura: 49]. Why? Because females were the type hated and unwanted in the Jahiliyyah: ﴿When one of them is given news of a female, his face darkens and he is filled with suppressed grief. He hides himself from the people because of the evil of what he has been given news of. Shall he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the dust? Surely evil is what they judge﴾ [al-Nahl: 58-59].

The matter did not stop at dislike of daughters; it went further to killing them and burying them alive, as He said: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked, for what sin she was killed﴾ [al-Takwir: 8-9]. This is because the girl is weak, unable to work, and does not take part in her people's constant wars, and she is a honour (ird) that must be guarded.

When Islam came, it completely changed this picture, raised the status of the female, and made women the counterparts of men. Therefore, here He placed females before males: ﴿He grants to whom He wills daughters, and He grants to whom He wills sons﴾ [al-Shura: 49]; and He softened the hearts of these harsh people toward the female, made them love her, and taught them that she is your vessel from which you came, so she is a source of merit over every male.

He taught them that the female's affairs in her society are not set right except when she is cared for, protected, and attended to by her guardian (wali); for dislike of the female drives her toward crookedness and compels her to abandon her role. When a girl is loved by her family, honoured and cherished by them, she grows accustomed to dignity and self-respect and does not accept humiliation from anyone, because she grew up knowing that she is precious to her family and dear to them, so no one dares to transgress against her even with a word.

In contrast is the girl who has been belittled by her family, who grew up among them amid feelings of hatred and contempt; we see her belittling herself, we see her cheap, squandering her dignity, and easily swayed even by a word.

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, raises His giving to the servant, saying: ﴿Or He gives them both males and females﴾. That is: He pairs the two kinds, so He grants you males and He grants you females.

﴿And He renders whom He wills barren﴾. That is: He withholds this gift for a wisdom that God intended.

So that no one boasts over another, and no one exalts himself over another, our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, teaches us that this matter of having children or not having children does not affect the ranks of His servants with God, the Exalted. When I grant males, or females, or pair them together, this does not mean My pleasure with My servant; and when I withhold it from him, this does not mean My anger with My servant. Rather, it is My sunnah (established way) in My creation: that I grant males, that I grant females, and that I render whom I will barren.

Therefore, you find this sunnah in force even among the messengers, who are the most honoured of creation before God. Our master Lot and our master Shu'ayb were granted daughters by God, our master Abraham was granted sons by God, and our master Muhammad (ﷺ) was granted sons and daughters, so he had ʿAbd Allah, al-Qasim, Ibrahim, Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah.

Thus: ﴿You have in the Messenger of God an excellent example﴾. And those who receive God's decrees in this matter with contentment, whose station of faith and submission is elevated, and who believe that this is a gift from God, even barrenness they regard as a gift, these God compensates. For instance, when you are content with daughters and raise them in the best upbringing, and treat them well, God will bring you, through their husbands, someone who compensates you for the lack of a son, and perhaps they will be more dutiful to you than sons are to their fathers.

The verse concludes with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful﴾. The All-Knowing gives according to the measure of His knowledge of affairs, and of what benefits His servant and what does not benefit him. He alone, glory be to Him, knows that this suits here and that suits there. Then He, glory be to Him, is All-Powerful, possessing absolute power in the matter of creation; nothing overcomes Him, and causes do not restrict Him.

Yes. These are three means, one of which must exist for God's communication with humankind to be completed. This is because humans have a created nature that cannot withstand direct contact with the Most High, glorified is He. God possesses the attributes of majesty and absolute perfection, and the Exalted cannot meet the lowly without intermediaries. Among them is inspiration (ilham), like the Psalms (al-Zabur) that was revealed to our master Dawud (David). It was not revealed to him as wahy from God through a messenger, as the Qur'an was revealed; rather, it came as inspiration that God cast into the heart (rawʿ) of our master Dawud.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿It is not for any human that God should speak to him except by inspiration, or from behind a veil...﴾ [al-Shura: 51], as He spoke to our master Musa (Moses). ﴿Or send a messenger...﴾ [al-Shura: 51], meaning: He sends him with the revelation. The messenger here is from among the angels, as God sent Jibril (Gabriel) with the Qur'an, even though he descended in the form of a human so as to be closer to them and more reassuring to them.

As for His saying ﴿except by inspiration...﴾ [al-Shura: 51], it means inspiration that God casts into the heart of whomever He wills. If you say: how do we recognize inspiration from the whisperings of Satan? They said: inspiration from God does not contradict itself by opposition; rather, it enters upon you as an established certainty with no dispute in it. We have also said that the incoming (warid) of the Most Merciful is never crowded out by the incoming of Satan.

We illustrated this with His saying, exalted is He, in the story of our master Musa and his mother: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Musa: suckle him, and when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him among the messengers﴾ [al-Qasas: 7].

This is wahy from God by way of inspiration. Therefore, the mother of Musa did not debate it or argue about it; rather, she set about carrying it out, content and reassured. Otherwise, what rational analogy would say to a mother: if you fear for your child, cast him into the river?

Here we mention a point raised by the orientalists, who tried to find a fault in the Qur'an by claiming it contains repetition, because the Most High said in another place: ﴿When We revealed to your mother what is revealed: "Cast him into the chest, then cast it into the river, and let the river deposit it on the bank, and an enemy to Me and an enemy to him will take him." And I cast upon you love from Me, so that you might be raised under My eye﴾ [Ta-Ha: 38-39].

Whoever reflects on the two passages will find that the first verse was a preface to the event, as evidenced by ﴿when you fear for him...﴾ [al-Qasas: 7], where "idha" refers to the future, whereas His saying ﴿"Cast him into the chest, then cast it into the river..."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 39] was the time of execution.

As for His saying ﴿or from behind a veil...﴾ [al-Shura: 51], we said: as God spoke to our master Musa, peace be upon him. ﴿Or send a messenger, and he reveals by His permission what He wills...﴾ [al-Shura: 51]. The revelation here is not inspiration like the first; rather, it is direct revelation through a messenger from among the angels, as happened in the descent of the noble Qur'an upon the heart of our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), through the trustworthy revealer Jibril. He would come to the Messenger of God directly and give him what God willed of the Qur'an.

However, God, exalted is He, wished to confirm this matter for them. So at times Jibril came to them in the form of a man of handsome appearance, showing no trace of travel, as is reported in the hadith, and he would question the Messenger of God and the Messenger would confirm him, so that people might learn from him the matters of religion. When he left, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "This was Jibril..." This is a matter by which we respond to those who asked that the messenger be an angel. For if the messenger came as an angel, he would come to them in the form of a man so that they could receive from him. Furthermore, the messenger is a model, an exemplar and a conduct, and exemplarity is not complete with angels, for if he said to me, "do such-and-such," I could say to him, "I am unable to do that; you are an angel and I am a human with limited capacity."

Therefore, we say that the Qur'an did not come as inspiration or as a breath cast into the heart, nor did it come from behind a veil; rather, it came by direct revelation through the angel, and the Messenger of God saw Jibril in his true form: ﴿And he saw him another time, at the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary﴾ [al-Najm: 13-14]. The matter of revelation and receiving from the Most High rests entirely on election: ﴿God chooses messengers from among the angels and from among humankind﴾ [al-Hajj: 75].

Not every angel receives from God; rather, only those whom God has chosen for that. Then He chooses from among humankind messengers who receive from the angel. The chosen among the angels, together with the chosen among humans, are able to receive from God. You will recall that we illustrated this with the "transformer" (al-tarans), i.e., the transformer that gives the device electricity according to its need and capacity; if the current rose, the device would burn out. Likewise, humans cannot receive from God directly.

Therefore the verse concludes with His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, He is Most High, Most Wise﴾ [al-Shura: 51], meaning: He is too exalted to address humans directly, for God is above that. ﴿Most Wise﴾ [al-Shura: 51] in His choosing of whom He selects to receive from Him, glorified is He.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 52:

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you﴾ [al-Shura: 52], referring to what was explained in the preceding verse of the three means of revelation. ﴿And thus We have revealed to you﴾ [al-Shura: 52], O Muhammad, ﴿a Spirit from Our command﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. The Spirit here is Jibril (peace be upon him), the trustworthy bearer of revelation. Allah named Jibril a "Spirit," just as He named the Qur'an itself a "Spirit," likening him to the spirit that the Truthful and Exalted One breathes into a human being, so that life and movement stir within him after he was a lump of flesh with no motion and no life.

You know that Allah created man from clay, then made his offspring from an extract of base water. When the fetus forms in its mother's womb, Allah sends to it an angel who breathes into it of His Spirit, Exalted is He, after 120 days from its conception, and life flows into it, the limbs function, and the organs move.

Just as the spirit is life for the bodies, the Qur'an is life for hearts and values. From here Allah named Jibril a "Spirit," and named the Qur'an a "Spirit." Among this is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life...﴾ [al-Anfal: 24].

The Truthful and Exalted One addresses them while they are alive with the life of the body and matter. So the life here is the life of the spirit and the heart, the life of values and principles, because the Truthful and Exalted One would not give His servant a spirit that moves his matter and directs his limbs, then leave his existence without a method, without values, and without morals.

Among the honor of man with Allah, Exalted is He, is that He grants him this spirit by which his heart, his values, and his morals live, because the life of the body and matter is a temporary, perishing life that passes away with the passing of the body.

As for the life of values and method, it is a lasting, enduring life that connects your life in this world with your life in the Hereafter. This is the life intended in His saying, Exalted and Glorified is He: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life...﴾ [al-Anfal: 24].

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith...﴾ [al-Shura: 52], meaning: you did not know anything about the Qur'an, or you did not know writing, and you did not know faith, meaning the detailed laws. We have said that illiteracy is an honor with regard to the Messenger of Allah, and an honor with regard to his community. Illiteracy is blameworthy except in the Messenger of Allah and in the community of the Messenger of Allah.

Had Muhammad been educated, reading and writing, they would have said that he brought the Qur'an from himself. And had his community been a community of learning and civilization, they would have said about Islam that it was a civilizational leap by which they wished to dominate the world.

So among the greatness of Muhammad is that his Lord says to him: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. It is related that the Caliph al-Ma'mun said to a man who wanted to insult him: "You are illiterate." The man said: "The Messenger of Allah was illiterate." Al-Ma'mun said to him: "Illiteracy in the Messenger of Allah is an honor, and in you it is a loss."

Therefore the Truthful and Exalted One commanded His Prophet in another place to say: ﴿Say: If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I had already lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then use your reason?﴾ [Yunus: 16].

Yes, where are your minds? Muhammad lived among you for a lifetime before the message, and you know him better than anyone, and you know that he was illiterate, unable to read or write, and you had never seen him as an orator or a poet. Therefore, out of their foolishness and obstinacy, they accused the Messenger of Allah of frequenting a foreign man who taught him the Qur'an. The Qur'an exposed their falsehood and said: ﴿The tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is clear Arabic speech﴾ [al-Nahl: 103].

So: nothing new that was not of human manufacture descended upon Muhammad. ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whomever We will of Our servants...﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. The word ﴿We made it﴾ [al-Shura: 52], that is, the Qur'an, ﴿a light﴾ [al-Shura: 52], a radiance that removes the darkness of ignorance and disbelief. This light is what guides whomever Allah wills to guidance, so that he walks upon the earth in guidance and insight, such that he does not collide with anything.

Collision means loss and destruction. If you collide with something stronger than you, it smashes you, and if you collide with something weaker than you, you smash it. Therefore we have said that in the reality of our lives we must keep some light. Even during sleep, we leave a faint lamp so that we may find our way in the darkness of night and not stumble when we rise at night.

From the light of matter we ascend to the light of the spirit and the heart, and to the method that illuminates our moral life. This is the light about which Allah said: ﴿And whoever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾ [al-Nur: 40].

We have said that a person illuminates his sphere of movement in life according to his capacity: one lights his life with a candle, another with a kerosene lamp, another with electricity, and so on. But when the sun shines, its light overshadows all lights, as if it were saying to us: extinguish your lights, for the light of Allah has come. When we ascend from material light to value-based light, we say: when the light of the method from Allah has come to you, cease all your methods.

And when the judgment from Allah has come to you, cease all your judgments, all your opinions, and your proposals. In the Sharia of Allah is what suffices you from all of this. Just as you do not need the light of your lamp during the day, so too you do not need any other method alongside the method of the Truthful and Exalted One, so be content with it instead of anything else.

When you compare the light of Allah with the light of men, the difference appears clearly, in material and spiritual light alike. You bring a candle, for example, and put a wick in it, and you bring matches to light it, and yet if a wind blows upon it, it goes out. The electric bulb needs tools to manufacture it and a transformer (trans) that regulates the electricity and the like, and after a month it needs a replacement, and if the current increases it burns out, and so on.

As for the sun, it illuminates the whole world. It does not require you to do anything, nor a spare part, nor maintenance. Moreover, your light lasts only as long as your life, whereas the light of the sun is lasting and permanent for as long as the universe endures and the world remains, from the time of Adam until the Hour is established.

Likewise the difference is clear in spiritual light. You see that the methods and laws of men are not free of errors and negative aspects. If they suit one group, they conflict with another group, and so you see them resorting to changing these laws from time to time. They are methods as deficient as human beings are deficient.

As for the methods of heaven, they are perfect, free of errors, taking into account all circumstances, and suitable for every time and every place, because they came from Allah, the All-Knowing of the condition of His creation, the All-Aware of what sets them right and what establishes their lives.

So: the Truthful and Exalted One would not grant us material light and deprive us of spiritual light, because it is more important and stronger in our lives than material light. Do you not see that the blind man can feel his way, and can bring someone to lead him and bring him to his destination?

As for one who has lost spiritual light, you see him stumbling in the labyrinths of life without guidance, and his state inevitably ends in perdition. Moreover, material light is tied to matter and perishes with its perishing, whereas the light of values is lasting, extending from this world to the Hereafter, and it is the foundation of the vicegerency on earth.

Therefore the Truthful and Exalted One explains this matter to us in Surat al-Nur, saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills, and Allah presents parables for the people, and Allah is Knowing of everything﴾ [al-Nur: 35].

The meaning of ﴿Light upon light﴾ [al-Nur: 35] is: the light of guidance and values upon the light of matter, so that you walk in your worldly life in guidance and insight, and are safe from deviation and misguidance in this world. Then this light brings you to safety and success in the Hereafter. This is the sense of ﴿and Allah presents parables for the people﴾ [al-Nur: 35], to clarify for them what was hidden from them. The material light is a sign of the spiritual, and the believer ascends from material light to spiritual light.

Then the Truthful and Exalted One explains the source of this light in the following verse: ﴿In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned; therein glorify Him in the mornings and the evenings﴾ [al-Nur: 36]. That is: O you who desire this spiritual light, seek it in the houses of Allah, for they are the source of its radiance. Seek it in prayer, in the remembrance of Allah, and in implementing the method that came to you from Allah.

So the Qur'an is a general light which, when we apply it, gives us another light, the light of acts of obedience and worship, and the most exalted source of this light is the mosque.

Therefore, when the scholars examined what the prepositional phrase in ﴿in houses...﴾ [al-Nur: 36] depends upon, they said it is connected to His saying ﴿Light upon light﴾ [al-Nur: 35], as if you were saying: light upon light in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised, which are the mosques. In these houses, the glorification of the morning is joined to the glorification of the evening. The people who frequent these mosques are described as ﴿men﴾ [al-Nur: 37]. Indeed, who are men if not these?

So: the Truthful and Exalted One gives us spiritual light embodied in His method, "do and do not do," and by this method human affairs of life are set right. But soon some of them fall into heedlessness, forgetfulness, or departure from this method, and they fall into disobedience, and new judgments and problems arise for them according to their departure and the corruption and violation of the method they commit.

Therefore we have seen that the messengers came one after another with progressive methods, each method suiting its people and correcting the ailments present in that time, although these laws all agreed in matters of creed and morals, and in the constants of religion such as prayer and zakat. Then after that the messenger came with specific rulings suited to the condition of his people and treating their diseases.

Whoever contemplates the procession of the messages finds that they develop in step with the movement of life and what arises in people's lives of new circumstances. For example, in the countryside we make between the fields a narrow path that can accommodate, say, one person passing or a loaded donkey, and they call it a "madaqq." Its purpose is that we reach our fields through it. But if we want a road between two villages, we widen it somewhat to accommodate a car, for example, and if it is between two cities it is wider.

Thus we have seen great development in the construction of roads, a development suited to the movement of life which has developed. Consider, for example, the Cairo–Alexandria desert road: you find it a broad, wide road to accommodate traffic on it, with two directions, going and returning, and it has rest stops with everything you need, because it is a long road.

The Truthful and Exalted One spoke to us about this matter, saying: ﴿He who made the earth for you as a cradle and threaded for you therein roads﴾ [Ta-Ha: 53]. When they wanted to lay out the city of Basra, Sayyidina 'Umar said to them: make the road wide enough for two loaded camels passing each other, and this is what we do in the modern age.

In Surat Saba' He said: ﴿And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed visible towns, and We determined therein the travel: "Travel therein by night and day in security."﴾ [Saba': 18].

The visible towns are the stations along the long road and the rest stops where you find what you need and rest. A long road must be divided into stages so that travel is comfortable and not arduous, and as the movement of life advances, these means advance with it, until we see in some rest stops places for rest and sleep.

Therefore the Truthful and Exalted One relates about those who transgressed and wronged themselves, among the notables and owners of luxurious vehicles, until they said: ﴿Our Lord, make the distances of our journeys far apart﴾ [Saba': 19]. Why, though travel and the length of travel are a hardship? They said: because they were wealthy people with vehicles not available to others. They wished thereby that no one other than themselves could travel, and that only the rich would take this road for trade.

This is also an example of progression in legislation. Whenever a new matter arises and new circumstances are found, legislation advances from one messenger to another to treat these circumstances, until the final legislation came, suitable for every time and every place, of which Allah said: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved Islam as a religion for you...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3].

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But We made it a light by which We guide whomever We will of Our servants. And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. The discourse here is about the Qur'an: Allah made it a light by which Allah guides whomever He wills of His servants. Thus He established that guidance belongs to Allah through this light sent down in the firm Book.

Then He also established guidance for the Messenger of Allah and entrusted him with legislating for the people, by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it...﴾ [al-Hashr: 7].

So the guidance of the Truthful and Exalted One is in the foundations and constants, which are what came in the verses of the Wise Reminder, and the guidance of the Messenger is in the branches, and in explaining and elaborating these foundations. If there arises in your lives something new, and matters come upon them for which no text has come, neither from the Book nor from the Sunnah, then unite your decision, and let the judgment be by consultation among you, and do not decide these matters by the opinion of an individual, but by the opinion of the community.

Therefore it is reported in the hadith... And how beautiful is what Shawqi, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

The opinion of the community: the lands do not suffer by it, despite disagreement; while the opinion of the individual makes them wretched.

Therefore they made consensus (ijma') the third source of Islamic legislation.

This verse established guidance to Allah, Exalted is He, through the Qur'an: ﴿But We made it a light by which We guide whomever We will of Our servants...﴾ [al-Shura: 52], and this is specific to the foundations and constants of religion for which there is an explicit text in the Book of Allah.

Then it also established guidance for the Messenger of Allah in the branches and in clarifying what was summarized in the Book of Allah: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. It gave our Master, the Messenger of Allah, the right and entrusted him with legislating for the people. Therefore his Sunnah (ﷺ) became the second source of legislation.

We have said that the guidance of the Truthful and Exalted One to the servant is guidance of clarification, instruction, and indication. If he obeys, he merits the guidance of success and assistance: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their consciousness of Allah﴾ [Muhammad: 17]. The guidance of the Messenger of Allah is only guidance of direction and clarification, and we have already explained this matter.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura: 52], meaning: you guide and indicate. The straight path is the upright, straight road that brings you to your goal in the quickest time, with the least effort and without hardship, because the road, whenever it bends, its time and hardship increase. Moreover, this path is a "sirat," meaning defined like a hair, and this means you must walk upon it with discipline, not deviating from it to the right or the left. Therefore He said in another place ﴿the even way﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 1], meaning its middle.

The straight path is the method brought by our master, the Messenger of Allah, a method that accompanies you in this world so that the affairs of your life are set right by it, and then gives you your reward in the Hereafter. Therefore the Truthful and Exalted One taught us to supplicate and say: ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor...﴾ [al-Fatihah: 6-7].

Then the Truthful and Exalted One clarifies the nature of this path:

﴿The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 42, verse 53:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, clarifies the nature of this path: "The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth..."

His saying, the Exalted: "the path of Allah." He attributed the path to Himself, so He is its Owner and its Lawgiver; it is not of your making. That is, the servant has no say in it. Since it is from Allah, you ought to follow it and beware of deviating from it.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, describes Himself with this attribute: "to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth." That is, the Owner of this path has dominion over what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, meaning in this world; then affairs will return to Him alone in the Hereafter.

"Surely to Allah all affairs are returned" (ala ila Allahi tasiru al-umur). This is a construction of exclusivity (qasr), meaning: to Allah alone, not to anyone other than Him.

So: this path and this method was set down for you by the One who owns this world and owns the Hereafter. Whoever walks on His method in this world will not be deprived of the reward in the Hereafter.

Thus the whole world is, from a beginning ("min"), heading toward an end, which is the Hereafter, and that end is to Allah alone. So between "min" and "ila," make your affairs good, for you are going from it to Allah. And remember that the abode of action is limited in time, while the abode of recompense is eternal and everlasting. This is an abode of hardship and toil, and that is an abode of bliss, "wherein is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived" (the hadith of the Prophet, ﷺ, in the Sahihayn, related from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him). "And whoever seeks the beautiful one, the dowry will make it costly."

Consider how this surah is concluded with His saying, the Exalted: "Surely to Allah all affairs are returned." "Ala" (surely) is a particle of alerting (tanbih), and alerting is only used for a matter of importance that deserves attention and must not be neglected. We have said: the speaker is the one who is aware of his speech and his time and does not neglect it, whereas the addressee may overlook what is said, so he needs alerting in important matters.

What is this important matter? It is "Surely to Allah all affairs are returned." This is a concise telegram at the close of the surah, which contains much meaning within it. Even among people, when a man advises his children before his death, for example, he does not advise them about every detail of the movement of life, but only about the important matters.

So His saying, glory be to Him, "Surely to Allah all affairs are returned," means: be alert that the whole matter is from Allah and to Allah: from Allah comes the method, and to Allah is the return and the destination.

So look at your conduct and make it conform to this method, and know that you are returning to Him, and your affair is heading to Him alone, for He, glory be to Him, did not create us in vain, and He will not leave us neglected. This is a truth that must never be absent from our minds.
